name: Design system starter
summary: Design system starter where design-system drift fails the build.
rules:
UI rules (design system v0)
- Style only with semantic tokens. No hex, rgb, px, ms or other raw values;
  allowed literals are inherit, currentColor, transparent, none, auto, 0, 1px, 100%.
- Compose system components and layout primitives, imported from src/index.ts.
  Never import radix-ui outside src/components or src/primitives, or
  react-aria-components and @internationalized/* outside src/components.
- Never restyle a system component with className or style. Need a new look?
  Propose a variant. UNSAFE_className / UNSAFE_style are escape hatches that need
  a lint disable with a reason, an owner and a removal condition.
- Before creating a component, walk the decision ladder: template → variant →
  component → primitive. Stop at the first yes.
- Missing token? Add a semantic token in tokens/ (with a dark value for colours),
  run npm run tokens. Never write a literal instead.
- New pages start from PageHeader (the one h1, status, actions) inside the right
  layout: AppShell for signed-in pages (fill its slots; never rebuild the frame),
  AuthLayout for signed-out pages, FocusedLayout for multi-step tasks; PageLayout
  for a page's sub-nav or aside. Copy the matching golden example: list → ListPage,
  record → RecordPage, create/edit → CreateEditFlow, settings → SettingsPage,
  sign-in → SignInPage, wizard → SetupWizard, dashboard → DashboardPage,
  queue/inbox → InboxPage, admin console → AdminConsole, error/404 → ErrorPages.
  Not other screens.
- Links go through Link (or Nav, NavTabs, Breadcrumbs); the app injects its router
  once with LinkProvider. NavTabs for sections that are routes, Tabs for panels in place.
- CSS: inside a declared @layer, BEM-lite classes, logical properties only,
  variants as closed data-* attributes, state via aria/native attributes,
  specificity ≤ 0,3,0, no !important, no ids.
- Every new variant, size or state gets a story. Every new exported component,
  layout or primitive gets a usage doc in docs/usage/<Name>.usage.tsx (when to
  use, when not to, do/don't, accessibility); tests/unit/docs.test.tsx fails
  without one. Lint, npm run check and the gallery (visual + axe + WCAG 2.2 checks) must pass.
- A story that renders an open modal is tagged ['modal-open', '!autodocs'].
- WCAG 2.2 AA is part of the gate: targets ≥ 24px or spaced (size.target-min),
  focus never hidden behind sticky content (scroll containers use
  space.scroll-padding.*), password fields as TextField type="password" with
  autoComplete (username, current-password or new-password, one-time-code),
  never block paste, pass AppShell's help from the shell composition, never
  ask twice in a multi-step flow, and any drag declares data-drag-alternative.
- Never add an eslint-disable or stylelint-disable without a reason after "--".
- Format every number, date, amount and list with useFormat() (LocaleProvider
  sets locale and time zone). Money is integer minor units + currency code.
- AI: render model output with StreamingText (never raw HTML), cite sources
  with Citation + SourcesList, mark unaccepted AI content with AiMarker, and
  never let AI write without ReviewChanges (or an explicit accept) and an Undo.
  The assistant acts only through the person's own can() and named mutations.
- Keyboard shortcuts go through useShortcut (never a bare keydown listener):
  every shortcut mirrors a visible control and shows its keys there (Tooltip
  shortcut, MenuItem.shortcut, Kbd). Reserved keys are refused and conflicts
  reported; single-key shortcuts can be turned off in the ? overlay.

Rewrite this platform's baselines (local ones are gitignored).
Build Storybook, then only the WCAG 2.2 checks (target size, focus not obscured, accessible authentication, consistent help) and their fixtures.

guides.title: Getting started
guides.summary: Five steps: bring the system in, load its styles once, render every signed-in page inside AppShell, route its links through your router, and set the reader’s locale.

guides.title: Principles
guides.summary: Three rules the whole system is built around. Each one is enforced by the build, not by review, so a change that breaks one fails before anyone has to spot it.

guides.title: Decision ladder
guides.summary: Before building anything new, walk the ladder from the top and stop at the first yes. Most needs stop at the first rung.

guides.title: Layout
guides.summary: Four layouts frame a page; eleven layout primitives arrange everything inside it. They take gaps, widths and ratios as tokens, so a layout can’t drift off the scale, and they hold no domain knowledge.

guides.title: Page archetypes
guides.summary: Most pages are one of a few archetypes. Each has one golden example: copy it, swap the nouns, keep the structure and the states. Don’t copy another screen.

guides.title: Data
guides.summary: The design system draws; the app layer knows. Everything about fetching, caching, validating and writing data lives in src/app, which the golden examples use and the system never imports.

guides.title: Accessibility
guides.summary: The target is WCAG 2.2 AA. The system guarantees what can be decided once; product code owns what depends on the page. Both halves are needed.

guides.title: Accessibility conformance
guides.summary: What the build checks against WCAG 2.2 AA, what it can’t, and how to run it. A green build is necessary for a conformance claim, never sufficient.

guides.title: Accessibility statement
guides.summary: A template for the statement a product publishes about its accessibility. Copy it, replace every [bracketed] part, and keep it true: a statement that overclaims is worse than none.

guides.title: Content
guides.summary: Plain, specific and calm. The words are part of the interface: a vague label or a blaming error is a defect like any other.

guides.title: Forms
guides.summary: Forms are among the most settled patterns in software, and breaking the conventions costs completions. Every control in the system shares one field anatomy, and the create-and-edit example shows the whole flow: validation on blur, an error summary on submit, a pending submit.

guides.title: Keyboard and power users
guides.summary: People who use a product all day stop reaching for the mouse. The system gives them a command palette, one registry for every shortcut, and pickers built for the keyboard, without taking anything away from people who find their way by looking.

guides.title: Motion
guides.summary: Motion gives feedback and shows where something came from. It is short, eased, built from tokens, and it gives way to the reduced-motion preference: nothing in the product depends on seeing it move.

guides.title: Theming and adding a brand
guides.summary: Every alternate look (dark mode, a rebrand, a customer’s colours) is a remap of the semantic token tier. Components read only semantic tokens, so a new theme is a list of values, never a change to a component.

guides.title: Escape hatches
guides.summary: Every system component and primitive takes UNSAFE_className and UNSAFE_style. They exist so a deadline never forces a fork, and they are loud on purpose.

guides.title: Contributing and versioning
guides.summary: Anything new starts as a proposal on the decision ladder, lands in one pull request with its stories, docs and tests, and leaves the old way through a deprecation, never a silent removal.

guides.title: Testing
guides.summary: The gallery is the test fixture. Every state gets a story, and every story is screenshotted in both themes, checked by axe and by the WCAG 2.2 checks, so a new state is covered the moment it has a story.

guides.title: Agents
guides.summary: Coding agents read the system from three files at the repo root, generated from the code. Point an agent at llms.txt first: it holds the rules and links to everything else.

guides.title: AI patterns
guides.summary: AI in this system is a set of shared parts, not a separate product: streaming answers, inline suggestions, citations, proposed changes with undo, and one assistant that acts only as the signed-in person. Define them once here so every team doesn’t invent its own.

foundations.title: Colour
foundations.summary: Every semantic colour role, in light and dark, with the contrast it is tested at. Values, pairs and ratios are read from the token source and the contrast check, so this page cannot drift from them.

foundations.title: Data visualisation
foundations.summary: Colours for chart marks: a categorical palette for series, a sequential ramp for magnitude and a diverging scale for polarity. Values, contrast and distances are computed from the token source by the same code the tests run, in both themes.

foundations.title: Typography
foundations.summary: Named text styles, each a complete font shorthand. Components pick a style; they never set a size, weight or line height on their own.

foundations.title: Spacing, sizing and radius
foundations.summary: Every length in the system comes from these scales. Layout primitives take the gap, inset and width tokens as typed props, so product code never writes a length.

foundations.title: Breakpoints and layout grid
foundations.summary: Layouts respond to the space they are given, not to the device. Two breakpoint tokens mark where the page frame changes; inside it, intrinsic layout primitives wrap and stack on their own, so there is no column grid to line things up against.

foundations.title: Elevation and motion
foundations.summary: Shadows say how far a surface floats; stacking tokens say what sits on top. Motion is short, eased and optional: every duration that isn’t the only sign of progress drops to zero under reduced motion.

foundations.title: Layers
foundations.summary: Seven stacking tiers, lowest first. Every z-index in the system is one of these tokens, and each kind of surface has one tier, so a menu never opens under a sticky header and a tooltip never hides behind a dialog.

foundations.title: Focus and target size
foundations.summary: Keyboard users need to see where they are; pointer and touch users need something big enough to hit. One focus ring for every focusable element, and one minimum size for every target.

foundations.title: Icons
foundations.summary: A small, closed set drawn on one 20-unit grid with one stroke token. Components take an icon by name; product code never imports an icon file.

exports.name: Accordion
exports.description: A stack of titled sections that open and close: steps an agent took, FAQ-style details. Each title is a heading wrapping a button with aria-expanded; arrow keys move between titles. From Radix Accordion. `single` (default) keeps one open; `multiple` lets several stay open.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of each item's title, so the outline stays right where it sits.

whenToUse: A stack of titled sections where people open one or a few: the steps an agent took, grouped settings help, an FAQ.
`single` (default) keeps one open; `multiple` lets several stay open. Set `headingLevel` to fit the page outline.

whenNotToUse.situation: Sections that are pages of their own

do.caption: Each title names a step and its status sits beside it.
do.code:
<Accordion
  defaultValue="check"
  items={[
    { value: 'search', title: 'Search records', meta: <Badge tone="success">Done</Badge>, content: '12 records matched.' },
    { value: 'check', title: 'Check permissions', meta: <Badge tone="success">Done</Badge>, content: 'You can move 10 of them.' },
  ]}
/>

dont.caption: Every section holds one line: show the lines instead.
dont.code:
<Accordion
  items={[
    { value: 'a', title: 'Owner', content: 'Sam Rivera' },
    { value: 'b', title: 'Status', content: 'Active' },
  ]}
/>

accessibility: Each title is a heading at `headingLevel` wrapping a button with `aria-expanded` (Radix Accordion). Arrow keys move between titles; Home and End jump.
A disabled item stays in the list and says why in its title or content.

exports.name: AccordionItem
exports.definition: interface AccordionItem { value: string; title: string; meta?: ReactNode; content: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean; }

exports.name: ActiveShortcut
exports.description: A registered shortcut, as the help overlay and the palette read it.
exports.definition: interface ActiveShortcut { id: string; keys: string; description: string; scope: string; characterKey: boolean; }

exports.name: AiMarker
exports.description: Marks content the AI wrote and a person hasn't accepted or edited yet: a sparkle and a text label on the AI tint. Never colour alone, and never on content a person wrote.

props.name: children
props.description: What the AI did, in words: "AI-generated", "Drafted with AI", "Suggested by AI". The text carries the meaning; the tint only reinforces it.

props.name: variant
props.description: badge: a pill beside a block or a field. inline: a quiet label inside a line of text or a header.

whenToUse: Content the AI wrote that a person hasn’t accepted or edited yet: a drafted field, a generated summary, a proposed change.
`badge` beside a block or field; `inline` in a header or a line of text (an assistant turn’s header).

whenNotToUse.situation: Content a person accepted or edited
whenNotToUse.instead: nothing: remove the mark, or record “edited” in the content’s history

whenNotToUse.situation: A button that runs an AI action
whenNotToUse.instead: a `Button` with the sparkle and a verb (“Suggest description”)

do.caption: The label says what the AI did; the tint and sparkle only reinforce it.
do.code:
<Cluster gap="sm">
  <Text as="span">Summary</Text>
  <AiMarker>Drafted with AI</AiMarker>
</Cluster>

dont.caption: A sparkle alone: colour and an icon aren’t a label, and it reads as decoration.

accessibility: The text is the meaning (WCAG 1.4.1): it is read with the content, and the tint only reinforces it. The sparkle icon is hidden from assistive technology.
Keep the label short and specific; it is read every time the content is.

exports.name: AppShell
exports.description: The app frame every signed-in page renders inside: skip link, sidebar (brand + nav), header (breadcrumbs, actions, account menu) and main. Pages fill its slots; they never rebuild the frame. The toast region is mounted here, once. Wide: a toggle at the foot of the sidebar collapses it to an icon rail (labels move into tooltips; accessible names stay). The choice is remembered in localStorage. Below the size.breakpoint.md container width the sidebar is replaced by a Menu button that opens the nav in a Drawer from the inline start: scrim, focus trap, Escape, focus return.

props.name: brand
props.description: Product name or mark at the top of the sidebar.

props.name: nav
props.description: Primary navigation: a <Nav label="Main">. It renders its own labelled nav landmark.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: Page trail in the header: <Breadcrumbs>. Omit on top-level pages.

props.name: actions
props.description: Global actions in the header (search, one global create). Never page navigation.

props.name: help
props.description: Help, in the same place on every page (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 Consistent Help): a Help menu with self-help and a way to contact a person. Rendered in the header, after the global actions and right before the account menu. Pass it from the app's one shell composition, never per page.

props.name: userMenu
props.description: Account menu, anchored at the header's inline end: <Menu trigger={…Avatar…}>.

props.name: children
props.description: The page. Rendered inside <main>, the only region that scrolls.

props.name: assistant
props.description: An assistant beside the page: an <AssistantPanel>. Wide, it is a column at main's inline end, under the header, and main keeps scrolling on its own; narrow, it gives way to a launcher in the header that opens the panel in a Drawer. Omit it and the frame is unchanged.

props.name: footer
props.description: Page action bar (a long form's Cancel · Save). Sticks to the bottom of main while the page scrolls. A submit button here reaches its form with the form="<form id>" attribute.

props.name: skipLinkLabel
props.description: First focusable element; jumps past the sidebar and header to main.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: Label of the button that opens the navigation drawer when the shell is too narrow to show the sidebar; also the drawer's name.

props.name: defaultNavOpen
props.description: Start with the narrow-screen navigation drawer open (gallery and tests).

props.name: sidebarCollapsed
props.description: Controlled: the wide-screen sidebar is collapsed to an icon rail. Pair with onSidebarCollapsedChange. A controlled shell does not write to storage; the owner does.

props.name: defaultSidebarCollapsed
props.description: Uncontrolled starting state, used when nothing is remembered yet.

props.name: sidebarStorageKey
props.description: localStorage key under which the uncontrolled collapsed state is remembered across visits. null turns remembering off (gallery and tests).

props.name: collapseSidebarLabel
props.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the rail toggle while the sidebar is expanded.

props.name: expandSidebarLabel
props.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the rail toggle while the sidebar is collapsed.

whenToUse: Every signed-in page. Define the composition once for the app (brand, nav, account menu); pages pass where they are and their content.
Fill the slots: `breadcrumbs`, `actions` (global only), `help`, `userMenu`, `children` (the page), `footer` (a long form’s action bar).
Pass `help` (a Help menu: self-help plus a way to reach a person) from the app’s one shell composition, so it sits in the same place on every page.
An assistant beside the page goes in `assistant` (an `AssistantPanel`): a resizable column at main’s inline end, a launcher in the header when narrow.
People can collapse the wide sidebar to an icon rail; the shell remembers it in localStorage under `sidebarStorageKey`. Give every primary nav item an `icon` so the rail reads well.

whenNotToUse.situation: Sign-in, sign-up and other signed-out pages
whenNotToUse.instead: a centred card without the shell
a proposal to extend AppShell; never a second frame

do.caption: The page fills main and uses the slots; the frame is untouched.
do.code:
<AppShell brand="Acme" nav={nav('Main (do example)')} breadcrumbs={<Breadcrumbs label="Breadcrumb (do example)" items={[{ label: 'Home', href: '/home' }]} current="Records" />} skipLinkLabel="Skip to content (do example)">
  <Center max="lg" gutters="md">
    <Stack gap="sm">
      <Heading level={3}>Records</Heading>
      <Text tone="muted">Only this region scrolls.</Text>
    </Stack>
  </Center>
</AppShell>

dont.caption: A page that rebuilds its own header and actions inside main: two headers, and page actions where global ones belong.
dont.code:
<AppShell brand="Acme" nav={nav('Main (don’t example)')} actions={<Button>Save record</Button>} skipLinkLabel="Skip to content (don’t example)">
  <Center max="lg" gutters="md">
    <Stack gap="sm">
      <Heading level={3}>Acme · Records</Heading>
      <Text tone="muted">A second title bar, typed again on every page.</Text>
    </Stack>
  </Center>
</AppShell>

accessibility: Provides the skip link, banner, navigation and main landmarks; `main` is the only scrolling region.
The collapsed sidebar opens as a drawer that traps focus and returns it to the Menu button.
The rail toggle has an accessible name that says what it will do, `aria-expanded` and a matching tooltip. In the rail, labels move into tooltips but stay each link’s accessible name.
Product code owns the page’s h1 and moving focus to it after client-side navigation.

The `help` slot always renders after the global actions and right before the account menu, the same relative order on every page (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 Consistent Help). The WCAG 2.2 checks fail an example page that renders the shell without it.
A sticky `footer` reserves `space.scroll-padding.end` in main, so a field that gets focus scrolls clear of the bar instead of under it (SC 2.4.11).

exports.name: AssistantPanel
exports.description: The assistant beside the page, in AppShell's `assistant` slot. Wide, it is a panel at the inline end that the person resizes (drag the edge, arrow keys on it, or Widen / Narrow) and closes to a launcher; the width is remembered. Narrow, it gives way to a launcher in the header that opens the same content in a Drawer. The content is mounted in one place at a time.

props.name: title
props.description: The assistant's name: the panel's landmark name and heading, the drawer's title ("Assistant"). Required.

props.name: children
props.description: The conversation: a ChatThread over a Composer, laid out to fill the panel.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled: the panel is open beside the page (wide) or in its drawer (narrow).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Uncontrolled starting state.

props.name: launcherLabel
props.description: Label of the button that opens it (a launcher at the edge when wide, in the header when narrow).

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions in the panel's header, before Close: New chat, a History menu.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: localStorage key under which the width a person chose is remembered across visits. null turns remembering off (gallery and tests).

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the resize handle.

props.name: defaultDrawerOpen
props.description: Start with the narrow-screen drawer open (gallery and tests).

whenToUse: An assistant that works beside the page it’s about (a record’s copilot): pass it as AppShell’s `assistant`, with a `ChatThread` over a `Composer` as its content.
People resize it (drag the edge, arrow keys on the edge, or Widen / Narrow) and close it to a launcher; the width is remembered under `storageKey`.

Below `size.breakpoint.md` it becomes a launcher in the header that opens the same content in a `Drawer`. Keep the conversation’s state in the page, not in the panel: the content moves between the two.

whenNotToUse.situation: A conversation that is the page
whenNotToUse.instead: a full chat page (the Assistant chat example) inside `AppShell`

whenNotToUse.situation: One AI suggestion inside a form
Details or filters for the page

do.caption: A thread over a composer, filling the panel; the page stays usable beside it.
do.code:
<AssistantPanel title="Assistant (do example)" storageKey={null}>
  <ChatThread label="Conversation (do example)" empty={<Text tone="muted">Ask about this record.</Text>} />
  <Composer label="Ask (do example)" onSend={() => undefined} />
</AssistantPanel>

dont.caption: A modal drawer for the assistant on a wide screen: it covers the page the answers are about.

accessibility: The panel is a complementary landmark named by its heading. Opening it moves focus into it; closing it returns focus to the launcher.

The resize edge is a focusable separator with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` (CSS pixels); arrow keys resize it (Shift for bigger steps), Home and End jump to the limits. Widen / Narrow is the single-pointer alternative to dragging (WCAG 2.5.7).
Narrow, the Drawer brings its focus trap, Escape and focus return.

exports.name: AuthLayout
exports.description: The frame for signed-out pages (sign-in, sign-up, password reset, an error before the app can load): a brand, one centred card on a plain surface, and a footer. No navigation, no shell.

props.name: brand
props.description: Product name or mark, above the card.

props.name: children
props.description: The card's content: the page's h1 first (a Heading at level 1), then the form.

props.name: footer
props.description: Links under the card: privacy, terms, help.

whenToUse: Every signed-out page: sign-in, sign-up, password reset, an emailed-link landing, a verification code step.
An error page shown when the app itself may have failed to load, so the shell can’t be relied on.
The card holds the page’s h1 first (a `Heading` at level 1), then one form; copy the Sign in example.

whenNotToUse.situation: A signed-in page, including a signed-in 404

do.caption: Brand above, one card with the h1 and the way in, legal links below.
do.code:
<AuthLayout brand="Acme" footer={<Text size="caption">Privacy · Terms</Text>}>
  <Stack gap="2xs">
    <Heading level={1} size={3}>
      Sign in to Acme
    </Heading>
    <Text tone="muted">Use your work account.</Text>
  </Stack>
  <Button>Continue with SSO</Button>
</AuthLayout>

dont.caption: Sign-in inside the app shell: navigation to pages the person can’t open yet, and a frame that implies they’re signed in.
dont.code:
<AppShell
  brand="Acme"
  nav={<Nav label="Main (don’t example)" sections={[{ items: [{ label: 'Home', href: '/home', icon: 'home' }] }]} />}
  skipLinkLabel="Skip to content (don’t example)"
  sidebarStorageKey={null}
>
  <Button>Continue with SSO</Button>
</AppShell>

accessibility: Provides banner (brand), main (the card) and contentinfo (footer) landmarks; the page supplies the one h1 inside the card.
The card never exceeds `size.content.xs` and reflows at 400% zoom; the page scrolls when the card is taller than the viewport.

exports.name: Avatar
exports.description: Showing who: record owners, activity authors, the signed-in user in the account menu trigger.

props.name: name
props.description: The person's name: the accessible name, and the source of the initials fallback. Required.

props.name: src
props.description: Photo URL. Falls back to initials when absent or when it fails to load.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Hide from assistive tech when the name is already visible beside the avatar.

whenToUse: Showing who: record owners, activity authors, the signed-in user in the account menu trigger.

whenNotToUse.situation: Representing a company, product or file
The only place a person’s name appears in a list
whenNotToUse.instead: the name as text, with the avatar beside it

do.caption: Beside the visible name, the avatar is `decorative`, so the name isn’t read twice.
do.code:
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Avatar name="Sam Rivera" size="sm" decorative />
  <Text as="span">Sam Rivera</Text>
</Cluster>

dont.caption: A row of initials with no names: people have to hover to find out who is who.
dont.code:
<Cluster gap="2xs">
  <Avatar name="Sam Rivera" size="sm" />
  <Avatar name="Alex Kim" size="sm" />
  <Avatar name="Jo Park" size="sm" />
</Cluster>

accessibility: `name` is required: it is the accessible name and the source of the initials fallback.
Set `decorative` when the name is already visible next to it.

exports.name: Badge
exports.description: A record’s status in a table row, title or card: a word plus a tone.

props.name: tone
props.description: Status tone. Map domain statuses to tones in one place; a new status extends the map, not the Badge.

props.name: indicator
props.description: Non-colour cue beside the text: a tone icon (default) or a dot.

props.name: children
props.description: Text label. Required: status is never conveyed by colour alone.

whenToUse: A record’s status in a table row, title or card: a word plus a tone.
Map domain statuses to tones in one place (the examples keep one status-to-tone map); a new status extends the map.

whenNotToUse.situation: A message that needs a sentence or an action
A count or a filter chip
whenNotToUse.instead: text, or a proposal for a new component

do.caption: One short word per status, the same word everywhere it appears.
do.code:
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Badge tone="success">Approved</Badge>
  <Badge tone="warning">Pending</Badge>
  <Badge tone="neutral">Draft</Badge>
</Cluster>

dont.caption: Sentences in badges, and a danger tone for something that isn’t a problem.

accessibility: Text is required: status is never colour alone, and tones add an icon or dot as a second cue.
Tone text meets 4.5:1 on its background in light and dark.

exports.name: Banner
exports.description: Ongoing state for a page or region: sits full width at the top of what it describes. Events get a Toast.

props.name: tone
props.description: Severity. Always shown as icon + text as well as colour.

props.name: title
props.description: Short bold lead ("Seat limit almost reached").

props.name: children
props.description: One sentence, or a list of links (an error summary).

props.name: action
props.description: The fixing action, as a Button ("Add seats", "Review import").

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows a dismiss button. The caller removes the banner.

props.name: announce
props.description: Live-region semantics by tone: danger and warning are role="alert" (assertive), info and success role="status" (polite). Render the banner when the condition starts; a banner present at page load is announced too, so keep load-time banners rare. Set false when focus moves to the banner instead (an error summary): announcing it as well would say it twice. A banner that isn't announced but has a title becomes a named region, so moving focus to it (with tabIndex={-1}) still tells assistive technology what it is.

whenToUse: A page-level message that stays until it is resolved: a failed load, a limit reached, an error summary after submit.
Put the fixing action in `action`.

whenNotToUse.instead: nothing in the product frame; they erode trust in real warnings

do.caption: What happened, then how to fix it, with the fix one click away.
do.code:
<Banner tone="warning" title="Seat limit almost reached" action={<Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Add seats</Button>}>
  9 of 10 seats are in use. New invites will fail at the limit.
</Banner>

dont.caption: A warning tone with no explanation or next step.

accessibility: Tone sets the live region: danger and warning are `role="alert"`, info and success `role="status"`.
Render the banner when the condition starts; one already present on page load is not announced.
Tone is shown as an icon and text as well as colour.

exports.name: Box
exports.description: Padding around content, from the inset scale: the box inside a region that has no component of its own (a toolbar strip, a panel's body). A surface with a border and a heading is a Card.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.

props.name: padding
props.description: Padding on every side. Token-typed: raw values are not accepted.

props.name: paddingBlock
props.description: Overrides `padding` on the block axis (top and bottom in horizontal writing).

props.name: paddingInline
props.description: Overrides `padding` on the inline axis (start and end).

whenToUse: Padding inside a region that has no component of its own: a toolbar strip, a panel’s body, the inside of a custom slot.
`padding` is an inset token; `paddingBlock` and `paddingInline` override one axis.

whenNotToUse.situation: A surface with a border, a heading or actions

whenNotToUse.instead: the `gap` of a `Stack`, `Cluster` or `Grid`: the parent owns the space between

do.caption: A toolbar strip padded from the inset scale.
do.code:
<Box paddingBlock="xs" paddingInline="md">
  <Cluster gap="sm">
    <Text size="caption">3 selected</Text>
  </Cluster>
</Box>

dont.caption: A Box wrapped around a Card’s body: the padding doubles up.

accessibility: Layout only: no role. Choose `as` for the semantics (`section`, `aside`) and name it when it is a landmark.

exports.name: BreadcrumbLink
exports.definition: interface BreadcrumbLink { label: string; href: string; }

exports.name: Breadcrumbs
exports.description: Path back up a genuinely nested hierarchy. A trail with no ancestors is decoration: leave it out.

props.name: items
props.description: Ancestors, outermost first. Every ancestor is a link.

props.name: current
props.description: The current page: plain text with aria-current="page". Matches the page title.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark.

whenToUse: Pages below the top level (a record, a settings category) in AppShell’s `breadcrumbs` slot.

whenNotToUse.situation: Top-level pages reached from the main nav
whenNotToUse.instead: no breadcrumbs; the nav already shows where you are
a heading that names the step

do.caption: Every ancestor is a link; the current page matches the page title.
do.code: <Breadcrumbs items={[{ label: 'Records', href: '/records' }]} current="Hardware lease" />

dont.caption: History instead of hierarchy: the trail repeats where you clicked, not where the page lives.
dont.code:
<Breadcrumbs
  label="Visited pages"
  items={[
    { label: 'Home', href: '/home' },
    { label: 'Search', href: '/search' },
    { label: 'Records', href: '/records' },
    { label: 'Search', href: '/search?q=lease' },
  ]}
  current="Hardware lease"
/>

accessibility: A labelled nav landmark with an ordered list; the current page is text with `aria-current="page"`.
Separators are decorative and hidden from assistive tech.

exports.name: Button
exports.description: To run an action on this page: save, create, delete, open a dialog.

props.name: children
props.description: Visible label. Required: icon-only buttons need `aria-label` and a Tooltip.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual intent. A new look is a new variant here, never a new component.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon from the system set. Decorative: the label remains the accessible name.

props.name: loading
props.description: Pending state: shows a spinner, keeps the label (so the accessible name survives) and blocks activation with aria-disabled, so focus is not lost.

whenToUse: To run an action on this page: save, create, delete, open a dialog.
One `primary` per view for the main next step; `secondary` for the rest; `ghost` in dense rows and toolbars.
`danger` for the action that destroys data, usually as the confirm button of a Dialog.

whenNotToUse.situation: Going to another page or record
whenNotToUse.instead: a link (`<a href>`), or a `Nav` or `Breadcrumbs` item

whenNotToUse.situation: Choosing one of several actions from a crowded header
Toggling a setting on or off

do.caption: One primary action, with the alternative as secondary. Labels are verb-first and say what happens.
do.code:
<Cluster gap="sm">
  <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  <Button>Create record</Button>
</Cluster>

dont.caption: Two primaries compete for the same attention, and "OK" doesn’t say what it does.

accessibility: A visible label is required; it is the accessible name. An icon-only button needs `aria-label` and a `Tooltip`.
`loading` keeps the button focusable and its name intact, and blocks activation with `aria-disabled`.
Defaults to `type="button"`; set `type="submit"` on the form’s submit button.

exports.name: Card
exports.description: A bounded surface for one titled block of a page: a record section, a settings group.

props.name: children
props.description: CardHeader, CardBody and CardFooter, in that order. Each is optional.

whenToUse: One titled block of a page: a record section, a settings category with its own Save.
Parts in order: `CardHeader` (title, description, small actions), `CardBody`, `CardFooter`.

whenNotToUse.situation: Wrapping a whole page or a table
whenNotToUse.instead: the page itself; a Table is already a surface
a `Stack`: a card without a title is just a box

do.caption: A titled section that saves on its own.
do.code:
<Card>
  <CardHeader title="Notifications" level={4} description="How we contact you about your records." />
  <CardBody>
    <Switch label="Email me a weekly digest" defaultChecked />
  </CardBody>
  <CardFooter>
    <Button>Save</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>

dont.caption: Cards nested in cards: the borders stack up and the hierarchy is lost.

accessibility: `CardHeader` requires a `title`, rendered as a heading at `level` (default 2) so the card is a section in the outline.
Keep the card’s actions inside it, next to what they affect.

props.name: justify
props.description: end: actions only. between: a status on the start side, actions on the end.

props.name: title
props.description: Section title. Required: a card without a title is just a box.

props.name: level
props.description: Outline level. Defaults to 2 (a section under the page's h1).

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the title: what the section controls.

props.name: actions
props.description: Small section-level actions, e.g. a ghost "Add" button.

exports.name: Center
exports.description: Horizontally centred column with a bounded measure.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum measure of the content.

props.name: gutters
props.description: Minimum space on either side when the viewport is narrower than `max`.

props.name: intrinsic
props.description: Also centre children on the inline axis (empty states, short messages).

whenToUse: The page column inside AppShell’s main: a bounded measure (`max`) with gutters.
`intrinsic` to centre short content such as an empty state.

whenNotToUse.situation: Centring one control in a row

whenNotToUse.instead: the page content directly in main

do.caption: A readable measure for running text.
do.code:
<Center max="sm" gutters="sm">
  <Text>Records track agreements from draft to renewal, with their owner, amount and every change along the way.</Text>
</Center>

dont.caption: An intrinsic centre around a long paragraph: centred text is hard to read.
dont.code:
<Center intrinsic>
  <EmptyState
    reason="first-use"
    headingLevel={4}
    title="About records"
    description="Records track agreements from draft to renewal, with their owner, amount and every change along the way, and can be exported."
  />
</Center>

accessibility: Layout only. Pass `as="main"` or `as="article"` only when that landmark isn’t already provided (AppShell provides main).

exports.name: ChangeOutcome
exports.description: How each change went once applied: done, or why it failed.
exports.definition: type ChangeOutcome = { ok: true; } | { ok: false; reason: string; }

exports.name: ChatThread
exports.description: The list of turns in a conversation. It follows new output while the person is at the bottom, stops following when they scroll up (and offers "Jump to latest"). Scrolling itself, it is a named, focusable region, so it scrolls from the keyboard. It is deliberately not a live region: each answer's StreamingText announces sentences, so tokens are never read one by one.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the thread ("Conversation about Master cleaning agreement"). Required.

props.name: children
props.description: The turns, oldest first: Message elements (give each a stable key).

props.name: empty
props.description: Shown instead of the thread when it has no turns: suggested prompts, not a blank box.

props.name: jumpLabel
props.description: Label of the button that returns to the newest turn after scrolling up.

props.name: scroll
props.description: self: the thread scrolls in its own region, filling its container (a panel). page: the thread grows and the page's scroll region (AppShell's main) scrolls; it follows the output there (a full chat page, with the Composer in AppShell's footer).

whenToUse: The scrolling list of turns in a conversation with an assistant: in an `AssistantPanel` beside the page, or a full chat page.
Give it the space to fill (a flex column); it follows new output while the person is at the bottom and offers “Jump to latest” when they scroll up.
Pass suggested prompts as `empty`, never a blank box.
On a full chat page set `scroll="page"`: the thread grows, AppShell’s main scrolls (the Composer goes in AppShell’s `footer`), and it follows the output there.

do.caption: An empty thread offers prompts to start from.
do.code:
<ChatThread
  label="Conversation"
  empty={<EmptyState reason="first-use" title="Ask about this record" description="Answers cite its fields and activity." action={<Button variant="secondary">When does it renew?</Button>} />}
/>

dont.caption: Turns stacked as paragraphs: no roles, no authors, nothing to navigate by.

accessibility: The thread is a named, focusable region (`label`), so it scrolls from the keyboard; turns are a list.
It is deliberately not a live region (`role="log"` would read every token): each answer’s `StreamingText` announces complete sentences instead.
Scrolling keeps focus clear of “Jump to latest” (`space.scroll-padding.end`).

exports.name: Checkbox
exports.description: An independent yes/no inside a form that is saved with the form.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name. Required.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive tech only, when the context makes it obvious visually: a row's checkbox in a table ("Select Hardware lease"). The name must still say what is selected.

whenToUse: An independent yes/no inside a form that is saved with the form.
Several independent choices from a short list; `indeterminate` for a “select all” parent.
Row selection in a table: `hideLabel`, with a label naming the row (“Select Hardware lease”), so the name still says what is ticked.

do.caption: Part of a form: nothing happens until Save.
do.code:
<Stack gap="md" align="start">
  <Checkbox label="Send a copy to the record owner" defaultChecked />
  <Button variant="secondary">Save</Button>
</Stack>

dont.caption: A negative label makes checked mean “no”. Phrase the option positively.

accessibility: `label` is required and clicking it toggles the box; `description` is linked to the control.
The mixed state is exposed as `aria-checked="mixed"`, not only drawn.

exports.name: Citation
exports.description: A numbered inline citation, [1], that follows through to its source in a SourcesList: activating it moves focus to that source. It is a real link, never an inert label.

props.name: number
props.description: The source's number, as it appears in the SourcesList (1-based).

props.name: sources
props.description: The `id` of the SourcesList this cites.

props.name: title
props.description: The source's title, for the accessible name ("Source 1: Renews on"). Required: a bare number means nothing when heard.

props.name: onActivate
props.description: Called when the citation is followed, with its number: highlight the source (and its passage) there.

whenToUse: An AI answer that makes claims: number each claim’s source inline ([1]) and list the sources under the answer, each with where it came from and a link to it.
Give the `SourcesList` a `useId()` id and pass it to every `Citation` as `sources`; `onActivate` highlights the source (and, in a record, the cited field).

do.caption: Each claim cites a source that says where it came from and links to it.
do.code:
<Stack gap="sm">
  <Text>
    It renews on 15 January 2027
    <Citation number={1} sources="usage-sources" title="Renews on" />.
  </Text>
  <SourcesList id="usage-sources" sources={[{ title: 'Renews on', origin: 'Record field', excerpt: '15 Jan 2027', href: '#properties', hrefLabel: 'Show in record' }]} />
</Stack>

dont.caption: An inert “[1]”: a citation that can’t be followed is decoration, not provenance.

accessibility: A citation is a real link named “Source 1: Renews on”, not the bare number; following it moves focus to the source, which is marked `aria-current`.
Citations sit inside running text, so the inline exception to the 24px target size applies; don’t use them as standalone controls.

exports.name: Cluster
exports.description: Horizontal group that wraps gracefully: toolbars, button rows, tag lists.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between items, both axes.

props.name: justify
props.description: Main-axis distribution. `between` gives a two-zone "title left, actions right" bar.

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis alignment.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wrap onto new lines when space runs out. Defaults to true.

whenToUse: A row that may wrap: buttons, filters, tags.
`justify="between"` for a two-zone bar: title on the start side, actions on the end.

whenNotToUse.situation: Items that must line up in columns across rows
Two regions of different weight, such as content and a rail

do.caption: A header bar: the title and its status on one side, the action on the other, wrapping on narrow screens.
do.code:
<Cluster justify="between">
  <Cluster gap="xs">
    <Heading level={4}>Hardware lease</Heading>
    <Badge tone="success">Approved</Badge>
  </Cluster>
  <Button variant="secondary">Edit</Button>
</Cluster>

dont.caption: Wrapping turned off for a long row: it overflows instead of reflowing.
dont.code:
<Cluster wrap={false} gap="xs">
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Status</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Owner</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Created</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Amount</Button>
</Cluster>

accessibility: Layout only. DOM order is visual order, including after wrapping.
For a list of items (tags, filters), render it as a list with `as="ul"`.

exports.name: CodeBlock
exports.description: Monospaced code in a keyboard-scrollable region: long lines scroll sideways instead of wrapping, so what is copied is what is shown. An optional language label and a CopyButton sit above it.

props.name: code
props.description: The code, shown exactly as given (leading and trailing blank lines are trimmed).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrollable region and context for the copy button ("Install command"). Required.

props.name: language
props.description: Language shown in the header ("bash", "tsx"). A label only: there is no syntax highlighting.

props.name: copyable
props.description: Show a Copy button.

whenToUse: Code, commands, config or payloads that people read or copy: API docs, setup steps, a webhook sample.
`label` names the region and the copy button (“Install command” → “Copy install command”). `language` is a label only; there is no syntax highlighting.

whenNotToUse.situation: A short value inline in a sentence
whenNotToUse.instead: `<code>` inside `Text`, with a `CopyButton` if it gets pasted

do.caption: A labelled block: long lines scroll sideways, and copy takes exactly what is shown.
do.code: <CodeBlock label="Install command" language="bash" code="npm install @acme/design-system" />

dont.caption: Code set in body text: it wraps, loses its spacing, and pasting it breaks.

accessibility: The code sits in a focusable `region` named by `label`, so keyboard users can scroll a long line (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`).
The copy button is a `CopyButton`: it announces “Copied” politely.

exports.name: Combobox
exports.description: A text field with a list of options that narrows as you type: choosing one value from many (an owner from 200 people, an account). Typing filters by a locale-aware "contains"; ↑ ↓ move, ↵ chooses, Esc closes. Behaviour, ARIA and focus come from React Aria's ComboBox.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name. Required.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen option's value, or null for none.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name: the chosen value is submitted.

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: Shown in the list when nothing matches what was typed.

props.name: showOptionsLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the button that opens the list.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Render the list open (gallery and tests).

whenToUse: Choosing one value from a list too long to scan (people, accounts, countries): type to narrow it.
A filter that picks one actor or one owner.

whenNotToUse.situation: Free text with suggestions, or jumping around the app

do.caption: A long list with a second line that tells similar names apart.
do.code: <Combobox label="Owner" options={PEOPLE} defaultValue="p02" />

dont.caption: Three options behind typing: a Select (or radios) shows them at once.
dont.code:
<Select
  label="Plan"
  options={[
    { value: 'free', label: 'Free' },
    { value: 'team', label: 'Team' },
    { value: 'enterprise', label: 'Enterprise' },
  ]}
/>

accessibility: React Aria’s combobox pattern: the input keeps focus, ↑ ↓ move through the list (announced), ↵ chooses, Esc closes; the button opens the list for pointer users.
Label, description and error are wired by React Aria’s slots and laid out like every other field.
Inside a Dialog the list portals into the dialog and Esc closes only the list.
Typing matches with a locale-aware “contains”, so accents and case don’t get in the way.

exports.name: ComboboxOption
exports.definition: interface ComboboxOption { value: string; label: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; }

exports.name: CommandGroup
exports.definition: interface CommandGroup { id: string; label: string; items: readonly CommandItem[]; filter?: 'local' | 'none'; }

exports.name: CommandItem
exports.definition: interface CommandItem { id: string; label: string; description?: string; icon?: IconName; keywords?: readonly string[]; shortcut?: string; onSelect: () => void; }

exports.name: CommandPalette
exports.description: The command palette: type to jump to a page or record or run an action. A modal dialog with the ARIA combobox pattern: the input keeps focus, ↑ ↓ move the active option (aria-activedescendant), ↵ runs it, Esc closes and focus returns. Results are grouped, ranked forgivingly, and their count is announced. Open it with ⌘K / Ctrl+K from the app's shell composition (useShortcut), and pass only what the person may do.

props.name: groups
props.description: Groups in order. A group with no matching items is left out.

props.name: query
props.description: Controlled query: pass it (and onQueryChange) when a group searches the server.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the dialog and the input.

props.name: loading
props.description: A group is still searching: shows a spinner in the input and says so in the count.

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: Shown when nothing matches.

props.name: countMessage
props.description: Announced as the results change: `(count) => '12 results'`.

props.name: maxPerGroup
props.description: The most items a local group shows for a query (all of them with an empty query).

props.name: platform
props.description: Override the detected platform for key hints (gallery and tests).

whenToUse: Once per app, in the shell composition, opened with ⌘K / Ctrl+K (`useShortcut` with `allowInInputs`) and from a Search button in the header that shows the keys.
Jumping to any page or record and running actions by typing: pages from the route table, records from a server search (`filter: "none"`), actions that mirror buttons.

whenNotToUse.instead: `SearchField` on the list page (its results stay in the page and the URL)

whenNotToUse.situation: Choosing a value for a form field
The only way to reach something
whenNotToUse.instead: visible navigation and buttons first; the palette is the fast path

do.caption: Grouped rows with a type in the description and a shortcut where one exists; only what this person may do is passed in.

dont.caption: A search button with no sign of the shortcut: pointer users never learn ⌘K exists. (And never pass rows the person can’t run: filter with `can` first.)

accessibility: A modal dialog (focus trapped, the page inert, Esc closes, focus returns) holding the ARIA combobox pattern: the input keeps focus and `aria-activedescendant` names the active option.
The number of results is announced (`role="status"`) as the query changes; `countMessage` words it.
↑ ↓ wrap around the list, ↵ runs the active row, and pointer users can click any row. Shortcuts on rows are also `aria-keyshortcuts`.
Keep labels verb-first for actions and give records a type in `description`, so a result is clear without seeing its group.

exports.name: Composer
exports.description: Where the person writes to the assistant: a text box that grows with its content, attachment chips, Send (or Stop while an answer arrives) and a keyboard hint. Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line, except while an IME composition is open.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the text box ("Ask about this record"). Required; shown only to assistive technology.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled text. Pair with onValueChange.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Send the message. Called with the trimmed text; the composer clears itself when uncontrolled.

props.name: streaming
props.description: An answer is arriving: Send becomes Stop, and Enter doesn't send. Typing the next question still works.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Stop the answer that is arriving.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Characters allowed. The count shows from 80% of it; over the limit, Send is disabled with the reason.

props.name: attachments
props.description: Chips for attached files, each with a Remove button.

props.name: onAttach
props.description: Shows an Attach button that opens the file picker.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The whole composer is unavailable (no permission, a hard limit reached). Say why in `note`.

props.name: note
props.default: 'AI can make mistakes. Check important info.'
props.description: A quiet line under the box: the disclaimer, or why it's disabled.

whenToUse: Where the person writes to an assistant, pinned under a `ChatThread`: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, and the box grows with its content.
Set `streaming` while an answer arrives: Send becomes Stop (`onStop`). Typing the next question still works.
Keep the disclaimer (`note`) unless the surface shows it elsewhere; set `maxLength` when the model has a limit.

do.caption: Labelled, with the keys and the disclaimer under it.
do.code: <Composer label="Ask about this record" placeholder="Ask about this record…" onSend={() => undefined} />

dont.caption: A one-line field with no Send button: multi-line questions are impossible and nothing says Enter sends.

accessibility: The text box is labelled (`label`, visually hidden) and described by the key hint; the count joins the description from 80% of `maxLength`.
Enter never sends during an IME composition. Over the limit, Send is disabled and the count says by how much; paste is never blocked.
Stop is always reachable while an answer arrives.

exports.name: ComposerAttachment
exports.definition: interface ComposerAttachment { id: string; name: string; }

exports.name: ContextMenu
exports.description: Actions on a thing, where the pointer or focus is: right-click (or Shift+F10 on the focused element). A shortcut to actions that are also visible somewhere (a ⋯ Menu, a toolbar): nobody discovers a context menu, so it must never be the only way. Items look and read like Menu's. Behaviour from Radix ContextMenu.

props.name: children
props.description: The region it belongs to: one focusable element (a row, a card). Right-click, a long press, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on it opens the menu.

props.name: items
props.description: The same entries as Menu: items (with an optional shortcut) and 'separator'.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional non-interactive heading (what the menu acts on).

whenToUse: A shortcut to the actions on a row, card or list item that are also available elsewhere (a ⋯ menu, a toolbar).

whenNotToUse.situation: The only way to reach an action
whenNotToUse.instead: a visible `Menu` on the thing: nobody discovers a context menu

whenNotToUse.situation: Overriding the browser’s menu on text, links or images
whenNotToUse.instead: leave the browser’s menu alone there

do.caption: The same items as the visible ⋯ menu, on a focusable region.
do.code: Northwind renewal More} items={[{ label: 'Archive' }, { label: 'Delete', tone: 'danger' }]} />

dont.caption: Actions that exist only on right-click: invisible to most people, and to keyboard users who don’t know Shift+F10.
dont.code: Report (no other way to delete it)

accessibility: Radix ContextMenu: opens on right-click, a long press, or Shift+F10 / the Menu key on the focused region; arrows, typeahead, Esc and focus return as in `Menu`.
The region must be focusable and named, so keyboard users can reach it.
Items look and read exactly like Menu’s, shortcuts included (`aria-keyshortcuts`).

exports.name: CopyButton
exports.description: Copies a value to the clipboard, confirms with "Copied" in place and a polite announcement, then reverts. If the browser blocks the clipboard it says so and asks the user to copy by hand.

props.name: text
props.description: The text put on the clipboard.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label.

props.name: accessibleName
props.description: Accessible name when the label alone is ambiguous, starting with the label so speech input still matches it ("Copy API key"). Defaults to the label.

props.name: copiedLabel
props.description: Label shown, and announced, after a successful copy.

props.name: failedMessage
props.default: 'Couldn’t copy. Select the text and copy it instead.'
props.description: Announced when the browser refuses the copy.

props.name: revertAfter
props.description: How long "Copied" shows before the button reverts, in milliseconds.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Called after a successful copy.

whenToUse: A value people paste elsewhere: an API key, an invite link, an ID, a command.
Set `accessibleName` when several copy buttons sit on one page (“Copy API key”); it starts with the visible label so voice control still matches.

whenNotToUse.instead: a `Button` that opens the share flow

do.caption: The value is visible, with a copy button beside it.
do.code: wsk_3f9a1c7e20b4

dont.caption: A generic button that copies silently: nobody knows whether it worked.

accessibility: On success the label reads “Copied” and a polite live region, present from mount, announces it; it reverts after `revertAfter` ms.
If the browser blocks the clipboard, it announces `failedMessage`, so keep the value visible and selectable.

exports.name: Cover
exports.description: Vertically centres its content in the available block size, with optional header and footer pinned to the edges. When the content is taller than the space, everything flows and scrolls.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.

props.name: header
props.description: Pinned to the block start (a brand).

props.name: footer
props.description: Pinned to the block end (legal links).

props.name: minBlockSize
props.description: fill: at least the parent's block size (the parent must have one). viewport: at least the viewport's.

props.name: gap
props.description: Minimum space between the header, the centred content and the footer.

whenToUse: Centring one block vertically in the space available, with an optional header and footer pinned to the edges: a sign-in card, a full-page message.
`minBlockSize="viewport"` for a whole page; `"fill"` (default) inside a parent that has a block size.
When the content is taller than the space, everything flows and scrolls; nothing is clipped.

whenNotToUse.instead: `AuthLayout`, which composes Cover with the brand, card and footer

whenNotToUse.situation: Centring horizontally with a bounded measure

do.caption: One message centred in the space, with a header pinned above it.
do.code:
<Cover header={<Text tone="muted">Acme</Text>}>
  <Stack gap="xs" align="center">
    <Heading level={4}>You’re all set</Heading>
    <Button>Go to Home</Button>
  </Stack>
</Cover>

dont.caption: Several unrelated blocks in one Cover: only one thing can be the centre of attention.
dont.code:
<Cover>
  <Stack gap="xs">
    <Heading level={4}>Recent records</Heading>
    <Heading level={4}>Usage this month</Heading>
    <Heading level={4}>Team</Heading>
  </Stack>
</Cover>

accessibility: Layout only: it adds no landmark. Pass landmark elements (`header`, `main`, `footer`) into its slots when it frames a whole page, as AuthLayout does.
DOM order is header, content, footer, so reading order matches what is seen.

exports.name: DateInput
exports.description: An instant (ISO timestamp, epoch ms or Date), or a calendar date with no zone ("2026-09-30").

exports.name: DatePicker
exports.description: A calendar date: typed segment by segment in the reader's locale order (from LocaleProvider), or picked from a calendar. Values are ISO strings ("2026-09-25"), calendar dates with no zone. Behaviour, ARIA and focus come from React Aria's DatePicker.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name: the ISO date is submitted.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name. Required.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest date that can be chosen (ISO).

props.name: max
props.description: Latest date that can be chosen (ISO).

props.name: calendarLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the button that opens the calendar.

props.name: previousMonthLabel
props.description: Previous and next month buttons.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Render the calendar open (gallery and tests).

whenToUse: A calendar date: a renewal, a due date, a birthday. Typed in the reader’s own order, or picked.
Values that are ISO calendar dates (“2026-09-25”), which is how the app passes them.

whenNotToUse.situation: A moment in time (with an hour)
whenNotToUse.instead: a date and a time, stored as an instant; show it with `useFormat().dateTime`

do.caption: Segments in the reader’s locale order (LocaleProvider), with the earliest allowed date set.
do.code: <DatePicker label="Renews on" defaultValue="2026-10-14" min="2026-09-25" />

dont.caption: A free-text date: ambiguous (is 03/04 March or April?) and parsed by hand.

accessibility: Each segment (day, month, year) is a spin button: type digits or use ↑ ↓; the calendar button opens a grid navigable with the arrow keys, Page Up/Down for months.
The locale comes from LocaleProvider, the same one `useFormat()` uses, so typed and displayed dates agree; the calendar opens on today in the provider’s time zone.
Inside a Dialog the calendar portals into it and Esc closes only the calendar.

exports.name: DateRange
exports.definition: interface DateRange { start: IsoDate; end: IsoDate; }

exports.name: DateRangePicker
exports.description: A range of calendar dates, start to end: typed or picked in one calendar. Values are ISO strings. To filter instants (an audit log's "from" and "to"), turn the range into the start of the first day and the end of the last in the reader's time zone, never UTC midnight.

props.name: startName
props.description: Form field names for the two ends.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name. Required.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest date that can be chosen (ISO).

props.name: max
props.description: Latest date that can be chosen (ISO).

props.name: calendarLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the button that opens the calendar.

props.name: previousMonthLabel
props.description: Previous and next month buttons.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Render the calendar open (gallery and tests).

whenToUse: A range of days: a report period, an audit log’s date filter, a leave request.

whenNotToUse.instead: `SegmentedControl` or `Select`, with a custom range as an option

do.caption: One field, one calendar: the two ends can’t be chosen out of order.
do.code: <DateRangePicker label="Date range" defaultValue={{ start: '2026-09-01', end: '2026-09-25' }} />

dont.caption: Two separate pickers: nothing stops an end before the start, and the range isn’t visible as one.

accessibility: Start and end are separate groups of segments with their own names; the calendar marks both ends and the days between.
Values are calendar dates. To filter instants, convert the range to the start of the first day and the end of the last in the reader’s time zone (as the audit log does), never UTC midnight.

exports.name: Dialog
exports.description: Modal dialog. Focus trap, Escape, scroll lock and focus return come from Radix Dialog.

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name and visible title. Required.

props.name: description
props.description: Short supporting text, announced with the title.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Element that opens the dialog, typically a system Button.

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions row. Put the primary action last.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Label of the close button (icon-only, so it needs a name).

whenToUse: Confirming a destructive or irreversible action (`size="sm"`, danger button that repeats the verb).
A quick create or edit of a light record: two or three fields.

whenNotToUse.instead: a full page from the Create and edit example

do.caption: A focused quick-create: a short title, the fields, and the primary action last.
do.code:
<Dialog
  title="New record"
  description="Records start as drafts."
  trigger={<Button icon="plus">New record</Button>}
  footer={
    <>
      <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
      <Button>Create record</Button>
    </>
  }
>
  <TextField label="Name" />
</Dialog>

dont.caption: A vague confirm: “Are you sure?” with “OK” forces people to reread what they clicked.
dont.code:
<Cluster>
  <Dialog
    size="sm"
    title="Are you sure?"
    trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete record</Button>}
    footer={
      <>
        <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
        <Button>OK</Button>
      </>
    }
  />
</Cluster>

accessibility: `title` is required and names the dialog; `description` is announced with it.
Focus moves into the dialog, is trapped there, and returns to the trigger on close. Escape closes it.
The close button is icon-only, so it has a name (`closeLabel`, default “Close”).

exports.name: Disclosure
exports.description: One section that shows and hides its details: an assistant's tool activity or reasoning, an advanced option. The toggle is a button with aria-expanded; from Radix Collapsible. For a stack of sections where opening one may close another, use Accordion.

props.name: summary
props.description: The always-visible summary, and the toggle's accessible name ("Searched 12 records"). Required.

props.name: meta
props.description: Beside the summary: a status Badge ("Done"), a count. Not part of the toggle.

props.name: children
props.description: What opens: tool input and output, reasoning steps, details.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Closed by default: details are there when wanted, not in the way.

whenToUse: One section of details people sometimes want: an assistant’s tool activity (what it searched, what it found), its reasoning, an advanced option.
Closed by default; the summary says what’s inside (“Searched 12 records”), with a status in `meta`.

whenNotToUse.situation: Several related sections, one open at a time

whenNotToUse.instead: show it; don’t hide it behind a toggle

do.caption: The summary says what happened; the details are one click away.
do.code:
<Disclosure summary="Searched records matching “overdue”" meta={<Badge tone="success">Done</Badge>}>
  <Text>12 records matched. 2 are archived and were left out.</Text>
</Disclosure>

dont.caption: A vague summary: nobody knows whether it’s worth opening.

accessibility: The toggle is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` (Radix Collapsible); Enter and Space toggle it.
Content that opens is in the reading order right after the toggle, so nothing is lost when it opens.

exports.name: Divider
exports.description: A hairline between blocks or inline groups. Prefer space (the gap of a Stack or Cluster) and headings to separate content; a line is for when space alone doesn't read as a boundary. Behaviour from Radix Separator.

props.name: decorative
props.description: true (the default): a visual line only, hidden from assistive technology. false: role="separator", for a line that divides groups of content people navigate between, such as groups of toolbar controls.

whenToUse: A boundary that space alone doesn’t make clear: between a form and its danger zone, between groups of toolbar controls.
`decorative` (the default) hides it from assistive technology. Set `decorative={false}` only when it divides groups people navigate between; it becomes a `separator`.

whenNotToUse.situation: Separating every item in a list or form
whenNotToUse.instead: the gap of a `Stack`, and headings for sections

do.caption: One line where the content changes kind.
do.code:
<Stack gap="md">
  <Text>Billing contact and invoices.</Text>
  <Divider />
  <Text>Danger zone: delete this workspace.</Text>
</Stack>

dont.caption: A line between every paragraph: the page turns into stripes and nothing stands out.

accessibility: Decorative dividers are hidden; semantic ones are `role="separator"` with their orientation. From Radix Separator.

exports.name: Drawer
exports.description: Modal side sheet over a scrim. Focus trap, Escape, scroll lock, outside click and focus return come from Radix Dialog; this component only lays it along an edge.

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name, and the visible title unless hideTitle. Required.

props.name: hideTitle
props.description: Keep the title as the accessible name but don't show it (a navigation drawer that shows the brand instead).

props.name: description
props.description: Short supporting text, announced with the title.

props.name: side
props.description: The edge it slides from. end (default) for details and filters; start for navigation.

props.name: size
props.description: Width: sm for navigation, md (default) for details and filters.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Element that opens the drawer, typically a system Button. It gets aria-expanded and aria-controls.

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions pinned to the bottom. Put the primary action last.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Label of the close button (icon-only, so it needs a name).

whenToUse: A side sheet over the page for work that needs the page as context: a record’s details from a list, a longer set of filters, navigation on a narrow screen.
`side="end"` (default) for details and filters; `side="start"` with `size="sm"` for navigation. AppShell already opens its nav this way on narrow screens.
Put the primary action last in `footer`; it stays pinned while the body scrolls.

whenNotToUse.situation: A short confirmation or a small form
Three or four quick filter options
Content people need beside the page while they keep working in it

do.caption: Filters in a drawer from the end, opened by a labelled button, applied from the footer.
do.code:
<Drawer
  title="Filters"
  description="Narrow the list. Applies when you choose Show."
  trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Filters</Button>}
  footer={<Button>Show 12 records</Button>}
>
  <Checkbox label="Active" defaultChecked />
</Drawer>

dont.caption: A confirmation in a drawer: a full-height sheet for one sentence and two buttons; a Dialog is the right size.
dont.code:
<Stack gap="xs" align="start">
  <Drawer title="Delete record?" description="This cannot be undone." trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete record</Button>} />
  <Dialog title="Delete record?" description="This cannot be undone." trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Dialog instead</Button>} />
</Stack>

accessibility: A modal dialog named by its required `title` (kept as the name when `hideTitle` hides it). Focus moves in, stays trapped, and returns to the trigger on close.
Escape, the close button (named by `closeLabel`) and a click on the scrim all close it; the page behind is inert.
The trigger gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` automatically.

exports.name: EmptyState
exports.description: What a list, table or panel shows instead of its content. Render it or the content, never both.

props.name: title
props.description: "Create your first record" · "No records match" · "Couldn't load records". Required.

props.name: description
props.description: One sentence: what fills this space, how to widen the search, or what failed.

props.name: action
props.description: One action. first-use: the same action as the page's primary button. no-results: clear filters. error: Retry.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Outline level of the title. Defaults to 2 (a region inside a page with an h1).

whenToUse: In place of a list or table that has nothing to show, with the `reason`: `first-use`, `no-results` or `error`.
Render it instead of the table, never beside an empty one.

whenNotToUse.situation: An error on a page that otherwise works

do.caption: Say what goes here and offer the one action that fills it.
do.code:
<EmptyState
  reason="first-use"
  headingLevel={4}
  title="Create your first record"
  description="Records track agreements from draft to renewal."
  action={<Button icon="plus">New record</Button>}
/>

dont.caption: A dead end: no explanation and no way forward.

accessibility: The title is a real heading (`headingLevel`, default 2) so the state is findable in the outline.
The icon is decorative; the title and description carry the meaning.

exports.name: EmptyStateReason
exports.description: Why the region is empty. Decide it from the unfiltered collection, never from the rows on screen: "nothing yet" and "nothing matches" need different words and a different action.

exports.name: EscapeHatch
exports.description: The only styling escape hatch on system components and primitives. The UNSAFE_ prefix makes every use greppable and countable. Consumer code must justify each use with an eslint-disable comment that carries a reason, an owner and a removal condition. A repeated override is a missing variant: propose one.
exports.definition: interface EscapeHatch { UNSAFE_className?: string; UNSAFE_style?: CSSProperties; }

exports.name: Feedback
exports.description: Thumbs up or down on one AI result, with an optional reason after a thumbs down. Both are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) with visible labels; a polite status confirms what was sent.

props.name: onFeedback
props.description: Called on a thumbs up at once, and on a thumbs down when the reason is sent or skipped.

props.name: label
props.description: Names what is being rated, for the group's accessible name ("Rate this answer").

props.name: reasons
props.description: Choices offered after a thumbs down. Keep them few and specific.

props.name: thanks
props.default: 'Thanks. Feedback helps us check and improve answers.'
props.description: Shown, and announced, once feedback is sent: say what it's for.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: A rating already given (a reloaded conversation).

whenToUse: Under an AI result (an answer, a summary, a suggestion) to learn whether it helped.
A thumbs down asks for a reason, which the person can skip. Say what feedback is for in `thanks`.

whenNotToUse.situation: Rating the product or a support conversation

whenNotToUse.instead: a “Report” action that reaches a person

do.caption: Two labelled toggles; the reason comes only after a thumbs down.
do.code: <Feedback onFeedback={() => undefined} />

dont.caption: Unlabelled buttons that don’t say whether anything was sent.

accessibility: Both are toggle buttons with visible labels (“Helpful”, “Not helpful”) and `aria-pressed`, in a group named by `label`.
A polite status, present from mount, announces the thanks once feedback is sent.

exports.name: FeedbackValue
exports.definition: interface FeedbackValue { rating: FeedbackRating; reason?: string; }

exports.name: FileRejection
exports.description: A picked or dropped file that broke a limit, with a message ready to show.
exports.definition: interface FileRejection { file: File; reason: 'type' | 'size'; message: string; }

exports.name: FileUpload
exports.description: Picks files with a button (the primary path) and, as an enhancement, accepts files dropped on its area. Shows the accepted types and size limit up front, then each file with its progress, its own error and a remove button. It validates type and size; the caller uploads.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and the group's accessible name ("Attachments"). Required.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting text above the limits.

props.name: error
props.description: Error for the field as a whole ("Add at least one file"). Errors about one file go on that file.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the Choose files button, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.

props.name: accept
props.description: Accepted types: extensions (".pdf") and MIME types ("image/png", "image/*"). Checked on pick and on drop.

props.name: acceptText
props.description: The accepted types in words, shown to everyone before they pick ("PDF, PNG or JPG").

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Largest file allowed, in bytes. Shown with the types.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allow more than one file per pick.

props.name: files
props.description: Files picked so far, with their progress and errors.

props.name: onFilesAdded
props.description: Called with the files that passed the limits and the ones that didn't.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Remove (or cancel) one file. Focus moves to the next file, or back to Choose files.

props.name: browseLabel
props.description: Label of the button that opens the file picker: the primary way in.

props.name: dropText
props.description: Text beside the button, for people who can drag.

whenToUse: Attaching files to a record or a form: contracts, receipts, images.

Say the limits before anyone picks: `acceptText` (“PDF, PNG or JPG”) and `maxSize`. Pass the same types as `accept`; the component checks type and size on pick and on drop, and hands you the accepted files and the rejections with ready-made messages.

You own the list: add accepted files to `files`, set `progress` while each uploads, set `error` on the one that failed, and remove on `onRemove`. Focus moves to the next file, or back to Choose files.

whenNotToUse.instead: a dedicated import flow (a `FocusedLayout` wizard) that maps columns and previews rows
the same component with `multiple={false}` and an image `accept`, previewed in a `Frame`

do.caption: The limits are visible up front; each file shows its own progress or its own error.
do.code:
<FileUpload
  label="Attachments"
  accept={['.pdf', 'image/png', 'image/jpeg']}
  acceptText="PDF, PNG or JPG"
  maxSize={10 * MB}
  files={[
    { id: '1', name: 'Signed contract.pdf', size: 2.4 * MB, progress: 40 },
    { id: '2', name: 'Survey scan.png', size: 14 * MB, error: 'Larger than 10 MB. Choose a smaller file.' },
  ]}
  onFilesAdded={noop}
  onRemove={noop}
/>

dont.caption: No limits until after the upload fails, and one error for the whole batch that doesn’t say which file.
dont.code: <FileUpload label="Attachments" error="Some files could not be uploaded." files={[]} onFilesAdded={noop} onRemove={noop} />

accessibility: The Choose files button is the primary path; dropping files on the area is an enhancement, declared with `data-drag-alternative` (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7).
A group named by the label. The button is described by the label, the limits and any error; `id` lands on it for an error summary link.
Adding files is announced politely (“2 files added, 1 file not added”). Each upload is a `Progress` named by the file.
Remove buttons are named per file (“Remove Signed contract.pdf”, “Cancel …” while uploading) and meet the 24px target size.

exports.name: FileUploadItem
