exports.description: A file in the list. The caller owns the list: it adds accepted files, reports progress and removes them.
exports.definition: interface FileUploadItem { id: string; name: string; size: number; progress?: number; error?: string; }

exports.name: FocusedLayout
exports.description: The frame for a focused, multi-step task (a setup wizard, a multi-step create): no sidebar, a header with the task and a way out, one centred column, and a sticky action bar. Only main scrolls.

props.name: brand
props.description: Product name or mark at the header's inline start.

props.name: task
props.description: The task, in the header ("Set up your workspace"). Plain text: the page's h1 is the step's PageHeader.

props.name: exit
props.description: The way out, at the header's inline end: a ghost Button or a Link ("Exit setup"). Required: a focused task never traps.

props.name: progress
props.description: A Progress bar under the header, across the column.

props.name: children
props.description: The content column: Stepper, PageHeader, the step's form.

props.name: footer
props.description: Action bar (Back · Next). Sticks to the bottom of main while the step scrolls.

whenToUse: A task that takes over the screen until it is done or abandoned: first-run setup, a multi-step create, a checkout.
The header names the task (plain text) and always offers `exit`; the column holds a `Stepper`, the step’s `PageHeader` and its form; `footer` holds Back · Next.
Copy the Setup wizard example.

whenNotToUse.instead: `AppShell` with its `footer` action bar (the Create and edit example)

do.caption: The task and a way out in the header; one column; the step actions in a sticky bar.
do.code:
<FocusedLayout
  brand="Acme"
  task="Set up your workspace"
  exit={<Button variant="ghost">Exit setup</Button>}
  footer={
    <Cluster justify="end">
      <Button>Next</Button>
    </Cluster>
  }
>
  <Stepper label="Setup steps (do example)" steps={steps} current={0} />
  <PageHeader title="Name your workspace" />
</FocusedLayout>

dont.caption: A wizard inside the app shell: the full navigation invites people to leave half-way, and nothing says how to exit safely.
dont.code:
<AppShell
  brand="Acme"
  nav={<Nav label="Main (don’t example)" sections={[{ items: [{ label: 'Home', href: '/home', icon: 'home' }] }]} />}
  skipLinkLabel="Skip to content (don’t example)"
  sidebarStorageKey={null}
>
  <Text>Step 1 of 3: Name your workspace</Text>
</AppShell>

accessibility: Provides banner (the header) and main landmarks; the step’s `PageHeader` is the page’s h1, and the task name in the header is not a heading.
The exit is required, so a focused task never traps anyone.
On a step change, move focus to the new step’s h1 (`PageHeader`’s `headingRef`), as the example does.

exports.name: Formatter
exports.definition: interface Formatter extends LocaleSettings { date: (value: DateInput, style?: DateStyle) => string; time: (value: DateInput) => string; dateTime: (value: DateInput, options?: { withZone?: boolean; }) => string; relative: (value: DateInput, now?: DateInput) => string; number: (value: number, options?: { maximumFractionDigits?: number; }) => string; percent: (value: number, options?: { maximumFractionDigits?: number; }) => string; compact: (value: number) => string; money: (minor: number, currency: string, options?: { compact?: boolean; }) => string; list: (items: readonly string[], type?: 'conjunction' | 'disjunction') => string; fileSize: (bytes: number) => string; }

exports.name: Frame
exports.description: Holds media (an img, video or iframe) to a fixed aspect ratio and crops it to fill, so a grid of thumbnails lines up whatever the source sizes. Other content is centred in the frame.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.

props.name: ratio
props.description: Aspect ratio the media is held to.

whenToUse: Media that must keep one shape whatever its source size: file previews, cover images, video, logos.
`ratio` is a token: `square` (avatars, logos), `landscape` (4:3, file previews), `wide` (16:9, video and covers). The media fills the frame and is cropped, never stretched.

whenNotToUse.instead: `Avatar`, which also falls back to initials

whenNotToUse.situation: Sizing a block that holds text
whenNotToUse.instead: let the text set the height

do.caption: Previews held to one ratio, so the grid lines up; the name beside each is its text.
do.code: {['Site plan.png', 'Floor two.png'].map((name) => ( {name} ))}

dont.caption: A bare image: a tall source makes a tall tile, and the grid breaks.
dont.code: Site plan.png

accessibility: Layout only. The media keeps its own alternative: `alt=""` when a visible name sits beside it, a real description when it carries information.

exports.name: Grid
exports.description: Auto-fit card grid: as many equal columns as fit, each at least `min` wide.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum item width. Columns are added or removed automatically, no breakpoints.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between cells.

whenToUse: Equal items that reflow by available width with no breakpoints: cards, stat tiles, galleries.

whenNotToUse.situation: A main region and a narrow side region

do.caption: Tiles of equal importance, each at least the `min` width.
do.code:
<Grid min="sm" gap="sm">
  {STATS.map((s) => (
    <Card key={s}>
      <CardHeader title={s} level={4} />
    </Card>
  ))}
</Grid>

dont.caption: A grid of one: an item that isn’t part of a set is just content.

accessibility: Layout only. Items read in DOM order, row by row.
For a set of like items, `as="ul"` exposes the count.

exports.name: Heading
exports.description: Page titles (`level={1}`, one per page) and section titles, in outline order.

props.name: level
props.description: Document outline level. Required: never skip levels to get a size.

props.name: size
props.description: Visual size, when it must differ from the level. Defaults to the level.

whenToUse: Page titles (`level={1}`, one per page) and section titles, in outline order.
When the look must differ from the outline, keep the right `level` and set `size`.

whenNotToUse.situation: Making text bigger or bolder for emphasis

whenNotToUse.instead: the `title` prop of `CardHeader` or `EmptyState`, which renders the heading for you

do.caption: Levels follow the outline; the section title is visually smaller with `size`, not a skipped level.
do.code:
<Stack gap="xs">
  <Heading level={3}>Billing</Heading>
  <Heading level={4} size={4}>
    Payment method
  </Heading>
  <Text tone="muted">Visa ending 4242</Text>
</Stack>

dont.caption: A heading used as a label for a value: it adds noise to the outline screen-reader users navigate by.

accessibility: `level` is required, so the outline is always a deliberate choice. Never skip a level to get a size.
Exactly one `level={1}` per page, matching the page title and the breadcrumb’s current item.

exports.name: HoverCard
exports.description: A supplementary preview of a link's destination, shown on hover and focus. Supplementary only: screen readers and touch never get it, so everything in it must also be at the destination. Behaviour from Radix HoverCard.

props.name: trigger
props.description: A link (or other focusable element) that already leads to the full content. The card opens on hover and on keyboard focus; it never opens on touch, so the trigger must work without it.

props.name: children
props.description: A preview of what the trigger leads to: a person's role, a record's status. Nothing interactive.

whenToUse: A preview of where a link goes: a person’s role and team behind their name, a record’s status behind its ID.
Supplementary only. It opens on hover and keyboard focus, never on touch, and screen readers don’t reach its content, so everything in it must also be on the page the trigger leads to.

whenNotToUse.situation: Anything people need to finish the task

do.caption: The trigger is a link to the full profile; the card previews it.
do.code:
<HoverCard trigger={<Link href="#people/priya">Priya Shah</Link>}>
  <Stack gap="2xs">
    <Text>Priya Shah</Text>
    <Text size="caption" tone="muted">
      Finance lead
    </Text>
  </Stack>
</HoverCard>

dont.caption: A trigger that goes nowhere, with the only copy of the approver’s decision in the card.
dont.code:
<HoverCard trigger={<Link href="#">Approval</Link>}>
  <Text>Rejected: the amount exceeds the budget.</Text>
</HoverCard>

accessibility: The trigger must be focusable (a `Link`); the card opens on focus and closes on blur and Escape.
The content isn’t focusable and isn’t announced. Keep it non-interactive and duplicated at the destination.

exports.name: Imposter
exports.description: Positions an overlay over the centre of its container, not the viewport: a notice over a chart with no data, a prompt over a locked panel. The container is the Imposter itself, so no positioning CSS is needed. For anything that must take focus and block the page, use Dialog.

props.name: children
props.description: The content underneath: what the overlay sits over.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.

props.name: overlay
props.description: What sits over the centre of the content: a notice, an upgrade prompt, a loading message.

props.name: contain
props.description: Keep the overlay inside the container, scrolling it if it is taller. Defaults to true.

props.name: overlayLabel
props.description: Names the overlay as a region and puts it in the tab order, so keyboard users can scroll it. Set it when a contained overlay can be taller than its container.

props.name: margin
props.description: Least space between the overlay and the container's edges.

props.name: inertContent
props.description: Makes the content underneath inert (not focusable, hidden from assistive technology) while the overlay covers it. Set it whenever the overlay hides what is underneath.

whenToUse: An overlay that belongs to one region, not the page: a notice over a chart with no data, an upgrade prompt over a locked panel, “Loading…” over stale content.
The Imposter is the container, so no positioning CSS is needed. `margin` keeps the overlay off the edges; `contain` (the default) keeps it inside and scrolls it if it is taller.
Set `inertContent` whenever the overlay hides what is underneath, so focus and screen readers skip it.

whenNotToUse.situation: Something that must take focus and block the page
A message that doesn’t cover anything
whenNotToUse.instead: `Banner` above the region, or `EmptyState` in place of it

do.caption: The locked panel is inert under the prompt, so nobody tabs into controls they can’t see.
do.code:
<Imposter inertContent overlay={<Banner tone="info" announce={false}>Usage history is on the Business plan.</Banner>}>
  {usageRows}
</Imposter>

dont.caption: An overlay without `inertContent`: the meters underneath are still read out and focusable.
dont.code:
<Card>
  <CardHeader title="Usage" level={3} />
  <CardBody>
    <Imposter overlay={<Text>Upgrade to see usage.</Text>}>{usageRows}</Imposter>
  </CardBody>
</Card>

accessibility: The overlay follows the content in DOM order and reading order.
`inertContent` sets `inert` on the content underneath while an overlay is shown.
A contained overlay that can be taller than its container needs `overlayLabel`: it becomes a named, focusable region so the keyboard can scroll it.

exports.name: InlineEdit
exports.description: A value you can change where it's shown: view → edit → save or cancel. Enter saves, Escape cancels, and focus returns to the value either way. Validation and the server's answer show under the field without losing what was typed. For one value at a time (a name, a title); a form with several fields is a form.

props.name: label
props.description: What the value is ("Name"). The field's label and the edit button's name ("Edit Name"). Required.

props.name: onSave
props.description: Save the new value. Return (or resolve to) an error message string to stay in edit mode with it; anything else means saved. While a returned promise is pending, Save shows its pending state; a rejected promise keeps edit mode with `failedMessage`.

props.name: validate
props.description: Check before saving: a message when the value can't be saved.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in view mode when the value is empty.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description: View only, with the reason as the edit button's description (no permission, archived…).

props.name: editLabel
props.description: Accessible names of the actions.

props.name: failedMessage
props.description: Shown when `onSave` throws or rejects.

props.name: defaultEditing
props.description: Start in edit mode (gallery and tests).

props.name: defaultDraft
props.description: Start in edit mode with this draft and its error (gallery and tests).

whenToUse: Changing one value where it’s shown: a record’s name in its header, a label in a table cell.
Frequent small edits by people who own the thing.

whenNotToUse.situation: A value that needs a long explanation or a review step
whenNotToUse.instead: a form with its description and a Save button

do.caption: The value is the edit button; Enter saves, Escape cancels, focus comes back to the value.
do.code: <InlineEdit label="Name" value="Northwind renewal" onSave={noop} />

dont.caption: An always-open field for a value people rarely change: it looks like a form waiting to be filled.

accessibility: View mode is a button named “Edit <label>: <value>”; edit mode is a labelled input with Save and Cancel buttons, so it works without the keys too.
Errors (from `validate` or returned by `onSave`) sit under the field, linked with aria-describedby; the draft is kept.
While `onSave`’s promise is pending, Save shows its pending state and Cancel is disabled.
`disabledReason` keeps the value visible and focusable, with the reason as its description.

exports.name: IsoDate
exports.description: A calendar date as the system passes it: ISO "2026-09-25", no time, no zone.

exports.name: Kbd
exports.description: A key or a keyboard shortcut, shown as key caps: in hints ("Tab to accept"), tooltips, menus, the command palette and the shortcuts overlay. `keys` takes shortcut notation and renders it for the platform (⌘K on a Mac, Ctrl K elsewhere); `children` names one key as printed. Symbols a screen reader would read badly (⌘, ↵) carry a spoken name. It only shows keys; register a shortcut with useShortcut.

props.name: platform
props.description: Override the detected platform (gallery and tests).

props.name: thenLabel
props.description: Word between the strokes of a sequence ("g i" → G then I).

props.name: keys
props.description: Shortcut notation: "mod+k", "shift+?", "g i" (a sequence), "j". `mod` is ⌘ on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere.

props.name: children
props.description: One key, named as printed on it: "Tab", "Esc", "Enter". For a hint in running text ("Tab to accept"); prefer `keys`, which also knows the platform, for a shortcut.

whenToUse: Showing a shortcut where people will learn it: a tooltip (`Tooltip shortcut`), a menu item (`MenuItem.shortcut`), a command palette row, the shortcuts overlay. Pass `keys` in shortcut notation (`mod+k`, `g i`).
Naming a key in a hint: “<Kbd>Tab</Kbd> to accept”, one Kbd per key (`children`, the key as printed).
`formatShortcut` where only a string fits; `ariaKeyShortcuts` for the `aria-keyshortcuts` attribute of a control the system doesn’t already set it on.

whenNotToUse.situation: Code, a command or a value to copy

whenNotToUse.instead: a `Button` whose label names the action; show the key beside it or in its tooltip

do.caption: Notation, not glyphs: `mod+k` shows ⌘K on a Mac and Ctrl K elsewhere, from the string the shortcut is registered with; a hint names its keys.
do.code:
<Cluster gap="md" align="center">
  <Tooltip content="Search and run commands" shortcut="mod+k">
    <Button variant="secondary" icon="search">
      Search
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
  <Text>
    <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> to accept · <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> to dismiss
  </Text>
</Cluster>

dont.caption: A combination typed into one cap, or a hard-coded ⌘: one strange key, wrong on Windows, and read as “place of interest sign”. Use `keys="shift+enter"`.

accessibility: Renders `<kbd>`. Symbols from `keys` (⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃ ↵ arrows) carry a visually hidden spoken name; with `children`, name keys with words people say (“Esc”, “Enter”).
Showing a shortcut isn’t announcing it: `Tooltip shortcut` and `MenuItem.shortcut` also set `aria-keyshortcuts` on the control.
A hint with keys needs a pointer path too: a visible button for the same action. Single-key shortcuts can be turned off (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.4) in the shortcuts overlay.

exports.name: KeyPlatform
exports.description: Where a shortcut is shown: Apple keyboards name modifiers with symbols (⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃), everyone else with words (Ctrl, Shift, Alt). `mod` is the platform's command key: ⌘ on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere.

exports.name: LayoutElement
exports.description: Elements a layout primitive may render as. Closed on purpose: layout, not widgets.

exports.name: Link
exports.description: An inline or standalone text link, styled from tokens and routed through LinkProvider.

props.name: href
props.description: Destination. Routed through the app's LinkProvider, when there is one.

props.name: children
props.description: Link text that makes sense out of context ("View invoice INV-2041", not "click here").

whenToUse: Navigation written as text: an inline link in a sentence, “View all records”, a way home from an error page.

Wrap the app once in `LinkProvider` (see Getting started) with its router’s link, adapted to take `href`. `Link`, `Nav`, `NavTabs` and `Breadcrumbs` then route client-side; without it they render a plain `<a>`.
The adapter spreads every prop onto its anchor and forwards `ref`: tooltips and focus management attach to it.

whenNotToUse.situation: An action that changes data or opens something in place
The app’s areas or a record’s sections
whenNotToUse.instead: `Nav` or `NavTabs`, which mark the current page

whenNotToUse.situation: A trail back up the hierarchy

do.caption: Link text that says where it goes, inside the sentence it belongs to.
do.code:
<Text>
  The lease renews in January. <Link href="/records/r-1002/files">Read the signed agreement</Link> for the full terms.
</Text>

dont.caption: “Click here”: out of context (a screen reader’s list of links) it says nothing about where it goes.
dont.code:
<Text>
  The lease renews in January. For the full terms, <Link href="/records/r-1002/files">click here</Link>.
</Text>

accessibility: A real anchor with an `href`, so it works with the keyboard, opens in a new tab and is listed as a link.
Underlined as well as coloured, so it never depends on colour alone.
Write link text that makes sense on its own; the page’s other links should not share it with a different destination.

exports.name: LinkComponent
exports.description: An app's router link, adapted to take `href`: React Router's `<Link to>`, Next's `<Link href>`.

exports.name: LinkComponentProps
exports.description: What the system hands an app's link component: every anchor prop, with `href` always set and `ref` included. The component must spread the rest onto its anchor and forward `ref` (tooltips and focus management attach to it).

exports.name: LinkProvider
exports.description: Injects the app's router link once, at the root. Every system link (Link, Nav, NavTabs, Breadcrumbs) then routes client-side. Without a provider they render a plain <a>.

props.name: component
props.description: The app's router link, adapted to LinkComponentProps.

exports.name: LocaleProvider
exports.description: Sets the locale and time zone every system and app format reads. Wrap the app once, near the root, with the signed-in user's settings. The formatting locale is separate from the UI language: an English UI can format German dates.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for formatting, from the user's profile (defaulting from the browser).

props.name: timeZone
props.description: IANA time zone, from the user's profile. Travelling users and shared screens break auto-detection.

whenToUse: Wrap the app once, near the root, with the signed-in user’s locale and time zone (a profile setting that defaults from the browser).

Format every number, date, amount, list and file size a person reads with `useFormat()`: `format.money(minor, currency)`, `format.date(iso)`, `format.relative(iso)`. One named format per concept keeps every screen consistent.
Money arrives as integer minor units plus an ISO 4217 code. Format the account’s currency in the reader’s locale: a German reader billed in USD sees `12.500,50 $`.
An ISO date with no time (`2026-09-30`) is a calendar date and never shifts by zone; a timestamp is an instant, shown in the provider’s time zone.
Outside React (tests, exports), `createFormatter({ locale, timeZone })` gives the same formats.
Turning typed money into minor units: multiply by `10 ** currencyDigits(code)` (2 for USD, 0 for JPY, 3 for BHD) and round.

whenNotToUse.situation: Dates and numbers in APIs, exports and logs
whenNotToUse.instead: ISO 8601 and plain numbers; format only for people
the app’s message catalogue; formatting locale and UI language are separate settings

whenNotToUse.situation: A one-off `Intl.NumberFormat` or `toFixed` in a page
whenNotToUse.instead: a named format here, or a new one added to it

do.caption: The value is formatted by the provider: the reader’s separators, the account’s currency.
do.code:
<LocaleProvider locale="de-DE" timeZone="Europe/Berlin">
  <Balance />
</LocaleProvider>

dont.caption: A hand-built string: US separators and a “$” for every reader, whatever the currency.

accessibility: Locale formats are what screen readers expect: “12.5%” and “Sep 12, 2026” are read naturally; “12.5 pct” and “09/12/26” are not.
Prefer month names over numeric dates in the UI: `03/04/2026` means different days in different regions.
Show relative times (“3 days ago”) with the absolute date nearby or on hover when precision matters.
Numbers in tables still need `numeric` cells, so digits line up in every locale.

exports.name: LocaleSettings
exports.description: Locale formatting over Intl. Every number, date, amount and list a user reads goes through one of these named formats, so the same concept looks the same on every screen and follows the reader's locale and time zone. No hand-built strings ("$" + n, toFixed, toISOString). Formatter instances are cached per locale and options: building one per table cell is slow.
exports.definition: interface LocaleSettings { locale: string; timeZone: string; }

exports.name: Menu
exports.description: Action menu. Keyboard, typeahead, focus return and ARIA come from Radix DropdownMenu.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Element that opens the menu, typically a system Button. It keeps its own accessible name.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional non-interactive heading at the top (the signed-in user in an account menu).

props.name: align
props.description: Edge of the trigger the menu lines up with.

whenToUse: Secondary actions behind a “More” button in a crowded header or table row.
The account menu in AppShell’s `userMenu` slot.

whenNotToUse.situation: Choosing a value for a form field

do.caption: The primary action stays visible; the rest live behind “More”, with the destructive one last.
do.code:
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Button>Edit</Button>
  <Menu
    trigger={<Button variant="secondary">More</Button>}
    items={[{ label: 'Duplicate record' }, { label: 'Export PDF', icon: 'download' }, 'separator', { label: 'Delete record' }]}
  />
</Cluster>

dont.caption: The main action hidden in a menu with a single item: one extra click for nothing.

accessibility: The trigger keeps its own accessible name and gets `aria-expanded`; arrow keys and typeahead move through items.
Focus returns to the trigger when the menu closes. Labels are verb-first, like buttons.

exports.name: MenuEntry
exports.description: An item, or 'separator' for a divider between groups.

exports.name: MenuItem
exports.definition: interface MenuItem { label: string; onSelect?: () => void; icon?: IconName; tone?: 'default' | 'danger'; disabled?: boolean; shortcut?: string; }

exports.name: Message
exports.description: One turn in a ChatThread: a header (who, when, the AI mark), the content, and actions (copy, retry, edit, feedback) once it has finished. User turns are tinted and aligned to the inline end; assistant turns run full width. Tool and system turns are compact notes. Render inside ChatThread.

props.name: author
props.description: Who it's from, shown in the header and naming the message ("You", "Assistant", "Search records").

props.name: time
props.description: When it was sent. Formatted with useFormat(); omit for pending turns.

props.name: status
props.description: An assistant turn's state: its actions show once it's no longer pending or streaming.

props.name: children
props.description: The content: StreamingText for assistant turns, text for user turns, a Disclosure for tool activity.

props.name: error
props.description: Why the turn failed, with the next step ("Too many requests. Try again in 30 seconds.").

props.name: copyText
props.description: The turn's text for Copy. Shows a Copy action.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Shows Retry (assistant: ask again; user: resend a failed message).

props.name: onEdit
props.description: Shows Edit on a user turn: puts its text back in the composer.

props.name: feedback
props.description: A Feedback control for an assistant turn.

props.name: marker
props.description: The AI mark on an assistant turn. Defaults to an AiMarker; pass null only where the whole surface is already marked.

props.name: stoppedLabel
props.description: Shown under a stopped turn, so it doesn't read as a finished answer.

whenToUse: One turn inside a `ChatThread`: `user` (tinted, at the inline end), `assistant` (full width, AI-marked), `tool` (what the assistant ran, usually a `Disclosure`) or `system` (a note such as “You stopped the answer”).
Actions appear once a turn has finished: Copy (`copyText`), Retry, Edit (user turns) and a `Feedback` control.

whenNotToUse.instead: the record page’s activity list (`Timeline` or the activity feed)

whenNotToUse.situation: A one-off AI result inside a form

do.caption: An assistant turn: who, when, the AI mark, the answer, then its actions.
do.code:
<Message role="assistant" author="Assistant" time="2026-09-14T10:04:05Z" copyText="It renews on 15 January 2027." onRetry={() => undefined} feedback={<Feedback onFeedback={() => undefined} />}>
  <StreamingText text="It renews on **15 January 2027**." />
</Message>

dont.caption: An answer as plain text with no author, time, mark or actions: it can’t be checked, copied or retried.

accessibility: Each turn is an `article` named by its author, so screen-reader users can move turn by turn.
An error shows as text with an icon (`role="alert"`) and a Retry; never colour alone.
The assistant avatar is decorative; the author name and the AI marker carry the meaning.

exports.name: MessageRole
exports.description: Who a turn is from: the person, the assistant, a tool the assistant ran, or the system (a note in the thread).

exports.name: Meter
exports.description: How much of a limit is used: seats, storage, API calls. Past a threshold it warns in words and an icon, not colour alone.

props.name: label
props.description: What is measured ("Seats", "Storage"). Visible; names the meter. Required.

props.name: max
props.description: The limit.

props.name: valueText
props.description: Usage in words, shown and read out ("42 of 50 seats"). Defaults to "value of max".

props.name: warningAt
props.description: From this value on the meter warns. Defaults to 80% of max.

props.name: dangerAt
props.description: From this value on the meter is in danger. Defaults to max (the limit is reached).

props.name: statusLabels
props.description: Words for each status beyond ok, shown with an icon and appended to the value text.

whenToUse: How much of a limit is used: seats, storage, API calls, a budget.
Say the usage in words with `valueText` (“42 of 50 seats”). Past `warningAt` (default 80%) it shows “Nearing limit”; from `dangerAt` (default the limit) “Limit reached”, each with an icon.

whenNotToUse.situation: A headline number with a trend

do.caption: Near the limit: the fill changes colour, and an icon and words say so.
do.code: <Meter label="Seats" value={42} max={50} valueText="42 of 50 seats" />

dont.caption: A progress bar for usage: it reads as a task heading for done, and never warns as the limit nears.
dont.code: <Progress label="Seats" value={42} max={50} valueText="42 of 50 seats" />

accessibility: A `meter` named by the visible label, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` (the usage, plus the status past a threshold).
Warning and danger are icon and words as well as colour.

exports.name: MultiSelect
exports.description: Choosing several values from a list that narrows as you type: tags, teams, event types in a filter. Chosen values show as removable chips in the field; the list stays open while you pick. Behaviour, ARIA and focus come from React Aria's ComboBox in multiple-selection mode.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name. Required.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen values, in the order they were chosen.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name: one value per chosen option is submitted.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of each chip's remove button: `(label) => 'Remove Legal'`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Render the list open (gallery and tests).

whenToUse: Choosing several values from a longer list: event types in a filter, tags, teams.
When the chosen values should stay visible (as chips) while more are added.

whenNotToUse.situation: A handful of options that fit on screen

do.caption: Chosen values as chips, each with its own remove button; the list narrows as you type.
do.code: <MultiSelect label="Events" options={EVENTS} defaultValue={['member.role_changed']} />

dont.caption: Two independent yes/no settings squeezed into a multi-select: checkboxes are clearer.
dont.code:
<Stack gap="xs">
  <Checkbox label="Email me" />
  <Checkbox label="Notify me in the app" />
</Stack>

accessibility: React Aria’s combobox in multiple-selection mode: options announce whether they’re selected, and the list stays open while you choose.
Each chip’s remove button is named after its value (`removeLabel`); removing one returns focus to the input.
The field wraps onto more lines rather than hiding chosen values behind a count.

exports.name: Nav
exports.description: Vertical navigation: the app's primary sidebar or a section sub-nav (settings). Grouped, data-driven.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark ("Main", "Settings"). Required: pages carry several navs.

props.name: current
props.description: href of the current page. That link gets aria-current="page", not only a heavier look.

props.name: onNavigate
props.description: Client-side routing hook. When set, a plain click calls it instead of following the link; modified clicks (new tab, new window) still use the browser. Apps with a router usually inject its link once with LinkProvider instead.

whenToUse: The app’s primary navigation in AppShell’s `nav` slot, defined once for the app.
A settings sub-nav grouped into Personal and Workspace sections.

whenNotToUse.situation: Switching views of one record in place
Showing where a page sits in the hierarchy

do.caption: A few top-level destinations, grouped, with the current page marked.
do.code:
<Nav
  label="Settings"
  current="/settings/profile"
  sections={[
    { label: 'Personal', items: [{ label: 'Profile', href: '/settings/profile' }, { label: 'Notifications', href: '/settings/notifications' }] },
    { label: 'Workspace', items: [{ label: 'General', href: '/settings/general' }] },
  ]}
/>

dont.caption: Actions dressed as destinations: “Export” and “Sign out” don’t lead to a page.
dont.code:
<Nav
  label="Records menu"
  current="/records"
  sections={[{ items: [{ label: 'Records', href: '/records' }, { label: 'Export', href: '/export' }, { label: 'Sign out', href: '/sign-out' }] }]}
/>

accessibility: `label` is required: pages carry several nav landmarks, and each needs a distinct name.
The current item gets `aria-current="page"`, not only a heavier look. Section labels name their lists.

exports.name: NavItem
exports.definition: interface NavItem { label: string; href: string; icon?: IconName; }

exports.name: NavSection
exports.definition: interface NavSection { label?: string; items: readonly NavItem[]; }

exports.name: NavTab
exports.definition: interface NavTab { label: string; href: string; }

exports.name: NavTabs
exports.description: Section navigation that looks like tabs but is links: each section is its own route. A labelled nav landmark with aria-current="page" on the current link, not an ARIA tablist.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark ("Record sections"). Required: pages carry several navs.

props.name: current
props.description: href of the current section. That link gets aria-current="page".

props.name: onNavigate
props.description: Client-side routing hook. When set, a plain click calls it instead of following the link; modified clicks (new tab, new window) still use the browser. Apps with a router usually inject its link once with LinkProvider instead.

whenToUse: Sections of a record or area that are each their own route: Overview, Activity, Files. The URL changes, the section can be bookmarked or opened in a new tab.
Tabs or NavTabs? If choosing one changes the URL, it is `NavTabs` (links, `aria-current="page"`). If it only swaps panels in place on one page, it is `Tabs` (an ARIA tablist).
Place it under the `PageHeader`, above the section’s content.

whenNotToUse.situation: Switching panels in place without changing the URL
Steps that must be done in order

do.caption: Each section is a route: links in a named nav, the current one marked with aria-current.
do.code: <NavTabs label="Record sections (do example)" items={sections} current="/records/r-1001/activity" />

dont.caption: An ARIA tablist for routes: screen readers announce tabs and panels, but each “tab” is really a page change.
dont.code:
<Tabs defaultValue="activity">
  <TabList label="Record sections (don’t example)">
    <Tab value="overview">Overview</Tab>
    <Tab value="activity">Activity</Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="overview">
    <Text>Loads /records/r-1001</Text>
  </TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="activity">
    <Text>Loads /records/r-1001/activity</Text>
  </TabPanel>
</Tabs>

accessibility: A `nav` landmark named by the required `label`, with `aria-current="page"` on the current link. It is not a tablist: Tab moves link to link, Enter follows.
The current section has a rule and a stronger colour, never colour alone.
On narrow screens the row scrolls sideways instead of wrapping; every link stays reachable by keyboard.
After a client-side section change, product code moves focus or announces the new section, as for any route change.

exports.name: NumberField
exports.description: A number typed in the reader's own format ("1.234,5" in German), parsed back to a number: amounts, quantities, percentages. ↑ ↓ step, Page Up/Down step by ten, Home/End go to min/max. Built on React Aria's NumberField (not a native number input, which takes "e", ignores the locale's grouping and changes on scroll). Formatting follows LocaleProvider, like useFormat().

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name. Required.

props.name: value
props.description: The number. With `currency`, integer minor units (cents), like every amount in the system: 125050 with "USD" shows $1,250.50. null is empty.

props.name: format
props.description: How it reads: a plain number, a percentage (0.25 shows 25%), or money when `currency` is set.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO 4217 code: the field shows and parses money, and `value` is in minor units.

props.name: step
props.description: Arrow keys and the stepper buttons move by this (in the value's units), and the value snaps to its multiples: leave it unset for money unless only whole units are allowed.

props.name: hideStepper
props.description: Hide the − and + buttons (arrow keys still step).

whenToUse: Quantities, amounts and percentages people type: seats, a price, a discount.
Money: pass `currency`, and the value is integer minor units, like every amount in the system.

whenNotToUse.situation: Numbers that aren’t quantities (a phone number, a postcode, an id)
A value from a small range, dragged

do.caption: An amount in the reader’s format, stored as minor units.
do.code: <NumberField label="Amount" currency="USD" defaultValue={125050} min={0} />

dont.caption: A text field for an amount: “1.250,50” and “1,250.50” can’t both be parsed, and nothing stops “12e3”.

accessibility: Why React Aria and not `<input type="number">`: the native input accepts “e”, ignores the locale’s grouping and decimal marks, changes on scroll, and its spinners are tiny targets.
Typing and display follow LocaleProvider (the same locale as `useFormat()`); ↑ ↓ step, Page Up/Down step by ten, Home/End jump to min/max.
The − and + buttons are 24px targets with names (`decrementLabel`, `incrementLabel`); they’re removed from the tab order, since the arrow keys do the same.

exports.name: PageHeader
exports.description: The top of every page: title (h1), optional status and description, and the page's actions. Breadcrumbs are not here: AppShell's header owns them.

props.name: title
props.description: The page title, rendered as the page's one h1. Matches the nav item or breadcrumb that leads here.

props.name: status
props.description: A status beside the title: a system Badge mapped from the domain status.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the title: what the page is for, or the record's key metadata.

props.name: actions
props.description: Page actions: secondary first, the one primary action last, then a "More" Menu. Right-aligned; they wrap.

props.name: headingRef
props.description: Ref to the h1, for moving focus to it after a client-side step or route change. When set, the heading takes tabIndex={-1} so it can receive focus without entering the tab order.

whenToUse: The top of every page, inside AppShell’s main or a FocusedLayout: the page title (the one h1), an optional status, one line of description and the page’s actions.
Actions go in `actions`: secondary first, the one primary action last, then a “More” `Menu` for the rest, destructive items last in it.
A record’s status goes in `status` as a `Badge`, mapped from the domain status in one place.

whenNotToUse.instead: AppShell’s `breadcrumbs` slot; the header of the frame owns the trail

whenNotToUse.situation: A section title inside the page

do.caption: Title, status and metadata on the start side; page actions on the end, primary last.
do.code:
<PageHeader
  title="Hardware lease"
  status={<Badge tone="info">Pending</Badge>}
  description="Owned by Facilities · updated 2026-09-10"
  actions={
    <>
      <Button variant="secondary">Share</Button>
      <Button>Request approval</Button>
    </>
  }
/>

dont.caption: A hand-built title row: the gaps, alignment and wrapping drift from page to page, and the status sits under the title.
dont.code:
<Stack gap="xs">
  <Heading level={1} size={3}>
    Hardware lease
  </Heading>
  <Badge tone="info">Pending</Badge>
  <Text tone="muted">Owned by Facilities</Text>
  <Button>Request approval</Button>
</Stack>

accessibility: Renders the page’s h1, so every page has exactly one, in the same place. Keep it the same words as the nav item or breadcrumb that leads here.
The status is a `Badge`: icon and text as well as colour.
Pass `headingRef` to move focus to the title after a client-side step or route change; the heading then takes `tabIndex={-1}`.

exports.name: PageLayout
exports.description: The regions of a page's body, below its PageHeader: an optional section nav at the inline start, the main column, and an optional aside at the inline end. When the container is narrower than size.breakpoint.sm the regions stack in reading order: nav, main, aside.

props.name: aside
props.description: Complementary content at the inline end: a record's properties rail. Rendered as <aside>.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the aside landmark ("Properties"). Required with `aside`.

props.name: children
props.description: The page's main column. A plain region: AppShell's <main> already contains it.

props.name: nav
props.description: Section navigation at the inline start: a <Nav label="…"> (a settings sub-nav). Nav renders its own labelled nav landmark, so this slot adds no landmark of its own.

whenToUse: The body of a page below its `PageHeader`, when the page has a second region: a record’s properties rail (`aside`) or a section sub-nav (`nav`).
`aside` is complementary content at the inline end, rendered as `<aside>` and named by the required `asideLabel`.
`nav` is section navigation at the inline start. Pass a `<Nav label="…">`: it is a nav landmark, not an aside, so the slot adds no landmark of its own.
Below the `size.breakpoint.sm` container width the regions stack in reading order: nav, main, aside.

whenNotToUse.instead: the page’s `Center` column and a `Stack`, with no PageLayout

whenNotToUse.situation: Two regions inside a card or a panel

do.caption: Main content first; the properties rail is a named aside at the inline end.
do.code:
<PageLayout
  aside={
    <Card>
      <CardHeader title="Properties" level={4} />
    </Card>
  }
  asideLabel="Properties (do example)"
>
  <Card>
    <CardBody>
      <Text>Summary, activity and files.</Text>
    </CardBody>
  </Card>
</PageLayout>

dont.caption: A sub-nav hand-placed with Sidebar and wrapped in an aside: navigation announced as complementary content, and a gap and width of its own.
dont.code:
<Sidebar
  as="aside"
  sideWidth="sm"
  side={<Nav label="Settings (don’t example)" sections={[{ items: [{ label: 'Profile', href: '/settings/profile' }] }]} />}
>
  <Card>
    <CardBody>
      <Text>Profile fields.</Text>
    </CardBody>
  </Card>
</Sidebar>

accessibility: The aside is a complementary landmark, and `asideLabel` is required whenever `aside` is set (a type error otherwise).
The nav slot relies on `Nav`’s own labelled nav landmark; nothing is nested or duplicated.
The main column is a plain region: the page is already inside AppShell’s `main`.
Regions stack in DOM order when narrow, so reading and focus order never change with width, and nothing is lost at 400% zoom.

exports.name: Pagination
exports.description: Moves through a long, server-paged list: a summary of what is shown, Previous and Next, and page numbers around the current one. A labelled nav landmark; the current page has aria-current="page".

props.name: page
props.description: Current page, from 1.

props.name: total
props.description: Total items across every page.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark.

props.name: pageLabel
props.description: Accessible name of a page button, from its number ("Page 3").

props.name: formatNumber
props.description: Formats counts in the summary. Defaults to the LocaleProvider's number format ("1,284", "1.284").

props.name: announce
props.description: Make the summary ("1–25 of 1,284") a polite live region, so a new page or a new total after filtering is announced. Use it when nothing else on the page announces the count.

whenToUse: Under a list or table that is paged on the server: it says what is shown (“1–25 of 1,284”) and moves between pages.
Reset to page 1 when the query or filters change. Set `announce` when nothing else on the page announces the new count.

whenNotToUse.situation: A short list that fits on one page
whenNotToUse.instead: no pagination; a count line if it helps

do.caption: What is shown, then Previous, the pages around the current one, and Next.
do.code: <Pagination page={12} pageSize={25} total={1284} onPageChange={() => undefined} />

dont.caption: Bare arrows: no page, no total, and no name for either button.

accessibility: A `nav` landmark (`label`, default “Pagination”); the current page has `aria-current="page"`, and each page button is named “Page n”.
At either end, Previous or Next is `aria-disabled` rather than disabled, so focus is never dropped from the button someone just used.
The current page is outlined and heavier, not only a different colour.

exports.name: Popover
exports.description: A small non-modal panel anchored to its trigger, for a few controls (a filter menu). Focus moves in on open and back to the trigger on close; Escape and an outside click close it. From Radix Popover.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the popover (it is a non-modal dialog): "Filter records". Required.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Element that opens it, typically a system Button. It gets aria-expanded and aria-controls.

props.name: children
props.description: A few controls that act on the page: filter checkboxes, a small form.

props.name: align
props.description: Edge of the trigger the popover lines up with.

whenToUse: A few controls anchored to the button that opens them, acting on the page as they change: a filter menu of checkboxes, a column picker.
It is non-modal: the page stays usable, Escape or a click outside closes it, and focus returns to the trigger.

whenNotToUse.situation: A hint on hover or focus
Many filters, or a form with a submit

do.caption: A Filters button that opens a named popover of status checkboxes.
do.code:
<Popover label="Filter by status (do example)" trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Filters</Button>}>
  <Checkbox label="Active" />
</Popover>

dont.caption: Controls in a tooltip: it vanishes when the pointer leaves, and keyboard users can’t reach what is inside.

accessibility: A dialog named by the required `label`; the trigger gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
Focus moves into it on open and back to the trigger on close; Escape closes it.

exports.name: Progress
exports.description: Determinate progress through a task: a bar with a label and the value in words. For work of unknown length use Spinner; for usage against a limit use Meter.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name ("Setup progress", "Uploading contract.pdf"). Required.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value, from 0 to max.

props.name: valueText
props.description: The value in words, shown beside the label and used as aria-valuetext ("Step 2 of 4", "3 of 12 files"). Defaults to a whole percentage.

whenToUse: Determinate progress through a task: steps of a wizard, files of an upload, rows of an import.
Say the value in words with `valueText` (“Step 2 of 4”, “3 of 12 files”); it is shown and read out. Without it, a whole percentage.

whenNotToUse.situation: Usage against a limit (seats, storage, API calls)

do.caption: A label and the value in words, over the bar.
do.code: <Progress label="Importing records" value={340} max={1284} valueText="340 of 1,284 records" />

dont.caption: A spinner for a job whose size is known: people can’t tell whether to wait or come back later.

accessibility: A `progressbar` named by the visible `label`, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` from `valueText`.
The bar isn’t announced as it moves. For a long job, announce milestones (a Toast when it finishes).

exports.name: ProposedChange
exports.description: One proposed change: a field's old and new value, or a text rewrite shown word by word.
exports.definition: interface ProposedChange { id: string; target: string; field: string; before: string; after: string; kind?: 'field' | 'text'; reason?: string; blockedReason?: string; }

exports.name: RadioGroup
exports.description: One choice from a few visible options (up to about five; more is a Select). Arrow keys move and select, Tab leaves the group: behaviour from Radix RadioGroup.

props.name: label
props.description: The question the options answer. Names the group. Required.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message for the group. Sets aria-invalid on the group.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the first option, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.

whenToUse: Choosing exactly one of two to about five options that are worth seeing side by side.
Add a `description` to options whose consequences differ.

do.caption: The group label asks the question; each option says what it means.
do.code:
<RadioGroup
  label="Billing period"
  defaultValue="yearly"
  options={[
    { value: 'monthly', label: 'Monthly', description: 'Cancel any time.' },
    { value: 'yearly', label: 'Yearly', description: 'Two months free.' },
  ]}
/>

dont.caption: Radio buttons for a long list: the form becomes a wall of options. Use a Select.
dont.code:
<RadioGroup
  label="Country"
  orientation="horizontal"
  options={['Austria', 'Belgium', 'Denmark', 'Finland', 'France', 'Germany', 'Ireland', 'Italy'].map((c) => ({ value: c, label: c }))}
/>

accessibility: Renders a labelled `radiogroup`; arrow keys move between options.
A group `error` sets `aria-invalid` on the group; pass `id` so an error summary can link to the first option.

exports.name: RadioOption
exports.definition: interface RadioOption { value: string; label: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; }

exports.name: Reel
exports.description: A single row that scrolls sideways, snapping to the start of each item: a strip of cards, thumbnails or suggestions that would otherwise wrap. The row is a named region in the tab order, so it scrolls with the arrow keys even when its items aren't focusable.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrolling region ("Recent files"). Required: the region takes keyboard focus.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between items.

props.name: itemWidth
props.description: Width of each item. `auto` lets each item size itself.

whenToUse: A row of like items that is fine to scroll sideways: recent files, suggested templates, image thumbnails.
`itemWidth` takes a grid-item token (or `auto`); items snap to their start as the row scrolls.
`label` names the row: it is a region in the tab order, so arrow keys scroll it even when the items aren’t focusable.

whenNotToUse.situation: Items people compare or must all see
Tabular data wider than the screen
whenNotToUse.instead: `Table` (its own scroll region, with a sticky header)

do.caption: A named row of recent files; the cut-off card at the edge shows there is more.
do.code:
<Reel label="Recent files" itemWidth="sm">
  {files.map((name) => (
    <Card key={name}>
      <CardHeader title={name} level={3} />
    </Card>
  ))}
</Reel>

dont.caption: Every file in a grid when only the latest few matter: the page grows with the folder.

accessibility: A `region` named by `label` with `tabIndex=0`: keyboard users can focus it and scroll with the arrow keys (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`).
Items are read in DOM order; snapping is `proximity`, never `mandatory`, so it never traps a scroll position.

exports.name: ReviewChanges
exports.description: Changes an AI proposes, reviewed before anything happens: each as a diff (a field's before and after, or a text rewrite word by word) with Accept and Reject, plus Accept all and Reject all. Only accepted changes are applied, then each shows its outcome and Undo restores the previous values. A change the person can't make says why instead of offering Accept.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the review ("Proposed changes to 6 records").

props.name: decisions
props.description: Controlled decisions. Undecided changes are left out: nothing is applied without a decision.

props.name: onApply
props.description: Apply the accepted changes (ids in list order).

props.name: applying
props.description: Applying: the button shows progress and the decisions lock.

props.name: outcomes
props.description: Once applied: each change's outcome by id. Shows the results and Undo.

props.name: onUndo
props.description: Restore what was there before. Shown once changes are applied.

props.name: undone
props.description: The applied changes were undone: says so, and the review is closed.

props.name: summary
props.description: Extra content under the heading: provenance ("Based on 42 records matching Overdue").

whenToUse: Before an AI changes anything: the proposed changes as diffs (a field’s before and after, or a text rewrite word by word), each accepted or rejected, then applied together.
After applying, pass `outcomes` (each change’s result) and `onUndo`: one Undo restores exactly what was there before.
Mark a change the person can’t make with `blockedReason` instead of hiding it, so the count adds up.

whenNotToUse.situation: A single suggestion inside a field
Changes a person made by hand
whenNotToUse.instead: the action itself, with a Toast and Undo

do.caption: Each change shows what it was, what it will be and why; nothing is applied until accepted.
do.code:
<ReviewChanges
  title="Proposed changes to 1 record"
  changes={[{ id: 'c1', target: 'Master cleaning agreement', field: 'Status', before: 'Overdue', after: 'Pending', reason: 'A signed renewal was added on 12 Sep.' }]}
  onApply={() => undefined}
/>

dont.caption: An AI action that applies at once with no preview: people can’t see what will change, or undo it.

accessibility: Removed and added text is struck through and underlined as well as tinted, and each carries a visually hidden “removed”/“added” (or “Was … will be …”), because screen readers don’t announce `del` and `ins`.
Accept and Reject are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) grouped per change and named by it; the count of accepted changes and the result after applying are polite status messages.

exports.name: SearchField
exports.description: A search input: type="search", a search icon, and a clear button once there is a query. Clearing (button or Escape) empties it and keeps focus in the field.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the input. Generated when omitted.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name ("Search records"). Required; hideLabel when the page makes it obvious.

props.name: value
props.description: The query. Controlled: results follow it as it changes.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the clear button.

whenToUse: Filtering a list or table by text as people type, in the list’s `role="search"` toolbar.
It is controlled: pass `value` and `onValueChange`, and derive the rows from the query. The clear button (and Escape) empty it and keep focus in the field.

whenNotToUse.situation: Picking one value from a known list

do.caption: A labelled search with a clear button once there is a query.
do.code: <SearchField label="Search records" value="lease" onValueChange={() => undefined} />

dont.caption: A plain text field for search: not announced as a search, no search icon, and no quick way to clear.

accessibility: `label` is required; `hideLabel` hides it visually only. The input is `type="search"`.
The clear button is named by `clearLabel` (“Clear search”) and is at least the minimum target size; clearing returns focus to the input.
Announce the result count elsewhere, once (a list’s `Pagination` with `announce`, or a polite status line), not on every keystroke from the field.

exports.name: SegmentedControl
exports.description: One value from a few, always exactly one, shown as joined segments: a date range, a view density. Radio semantics (Radix RadioGroup): a named radiogroup of radios; Tab enters at the checked one, arrow keys move and select.

props.name: label
props.description: The question the options answer ("Date range"). Names the group. Required.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Hide the label visually when the options explain themselves; it stays the group's name.

props.name: options
props.description: Two to five options.

whenToUse: Choosing one of two to five short options that change what the page shows, where one is always chosen: a date range, a density, list or board.

It is a radio group underneath (a named radiogroup of radios), because exactly one value is always selected and it can’t be cleared. Tab reaches the checked option; arrow keys move and select at once.

whenNotToUse.situation: A choice inside a form that is submitted
More than five options, or long labels

do.caption: A named group of short, parallel options with one always selected.
do.code: <SegmentedControl label="Date range (do example)" options={ranges} defaultValue="30d" />

dont.caption: A row of buttons faking a selection: nothing tells assistive tech which one is chosen, or that they belong together.
dont.code:
<Cluster gap="2xs">
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
    7 days
  </Button>
  <Button size="sm">30 days</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
    90 days
  </Button>
</Cluster>

accessibility: `label` is required and names the group; `hideLabel` hides it visually only.
The checked segment is raised, outlined and heavier, not just a different colour.
Arrow keys select as they move (selection follows focus), so each move updates the page: keep the update fast and don’t move focus.

exports.name: SegmentedOption
exports.definition: interface SegmentedOption { value: string; label: string; }

exports.name: Select
exports.description: Single-choice list. Behaviour (keyboard, typeahead, focus, ARIA) comes from Radix Select.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name of the trigger. Required.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name; a hidden native select carries the value in forms.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Render the list open (gallery and tests).

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the trigger, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.

whenToUse: Choosing one option from a list of about five or more, where showing them all would crowd the form.

whenNotToUse.situation: Two to four options that benefit from being compared

do.caption: Many options, a clear label, and a sensible default.
do.code: <Select label="Status" options={STATUSES} defaultValue="draft" />

dont.caption: Two options hidden behind a click. Radio buttons show both at once.
dont.code:
<Select
  label="Billing"
  options={[
    { value: 'monthly', label: 'Monthly' },
    { value: 'yearly', label: 'Yearly' },
  ]}
  placeholder="Choose"
/>

accessibility: Keyboard, typeahead and focus return come from Radix; the trigger’s accessible name is the `label`.
A hidden native select carries the value, so `name` works inside a form.

exports.name: SelectOption
exports.definition: interface SelectOption { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean; }

exports.name: ShortcutConflict
exports.definition: interface ShortcutConflict { keys: string; kept: string; refused: string; }

exports.name: ShortcutDefinition
exports.definition: interface ShortcutDefinition { id: string; keys: string; description: string; scope?: string; handler: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void; allowInInputs?: boolean; allowInDialogs?: boolean; enabled?: boolean; }

exports.name: ShortcutHelp
exports.description: The shortcuts overlay: every active shortcut, grouped by scope, with its keys. Mount it once in the app's shell composition; it registers its own key (?) and lists whatever else is registered while it's open, so a page's shortcuts appear on that page only. It also holds the switch that turns single-key shortcuts off.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Optional element that opens it (a Help menu item opens it with `open` instead).

props.name: keys
props.description: Keys that open it. Default "?" (Shift+/).

props.name: platform
props.description: Override the detected platform (gallery and tests).

whenToUse: `useShortcut` for every keyboard shortcut: global ones in the app’s shell composition, page ones in the page, so they register and unregister with it.
`ShortcutHelp` once, in the shell composition: `?` opens it, and it lists every shortcut active right now, by scope.
A shortcut for something people repeat all day (move through a list, triage, open the palette), always mirroring a visible control.

whenNotToUse.situation: The only way to reach an action
whenNotToUse.instead: a visible button or menu item first; the shortcut is the accelerator

whenNotToUse.situation: A key the browser or a screen reader owns (copy, find, Tab, arrows, Escape, Control+Option…)
whenNotToUse.instead: another key: the registry refuses reserved keys

whenNotToUse.situation: Keys inside one widget (arrows in a listbox, Enter in a field)
whenNotToUse.instead: the widget’s own key handling; the registry is for page and app shortcuts

do.caption: One entry point for help, reachable by pointer too; shortcuts registered with a scope and a verb-first description.
do.code: <ShortcutHelp trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Keyboard shortcuts</Button>} />

dont.caption: A bare document keydown listener: invisible in the help overlay, unaware of text fields and dialogs, free to steal keys from assistive technology.
dont.code: <Button variant="secondary">Archive (press E; no one can find out)</Button>

accessibility: Nothing fires while typing in a field (unless the shortcut sets `allowInInputs`, as ⌘K does), inside a dialog (unless `allowInDialogs`), during IME composition, or after another handler took the key.
Single-key shortcuts can be turned off in the overlay (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.4, Character Key Shortcuts); the choice is remembered on this device.
Reserved keys are refused and conflicts are reported (the first registration keeps its keys), so a feature can’t silently break another or the browser.
Pair each shortcut with a visible control that shows it (`Tooltip shortcut`, `MenuItem.shortcut`): shortcuts are accelerators, never the only path.

exports.name: Sidebar
exports.description: Side region beside main content. When the content would drop below half the container, the two stack. No media query: it responds to its container.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.

props.name: side
props.description: Content of the narrow side region.

props.name: placement
props.description: Which edge the side region sits on. DOM order follows, so reading order matches.

props.name: sideWidth
props.description: Preferred width of the side region.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between the regions.

whenToUse: A narrow region beside a wider one inside a card, panel or dialog, stacking when space runs out.
`placement` sets the edge; DOM order follows, so reading order matches.

whenNotToUse.instead: AppShell, which owns it and collapses it to a drawer

whenNotToUse.situation: A page’s properties rail or section sub-nav
whenNotToUse.instead: `PageLayout`, which names the aside and places the nav

do.caption: Main content first, a narrow region at the end that stacks below it when space runs out.
do.code:
<Sidebar
  placement="end"
  sideWidth="sm"
  gap="md"
  side={
    <Card>
      <CardHeader title="Properties" level={4} />
    </Card>
  }
>
  <Card>
    <CardBody>
      <Text>Activity, newest first.</Text>
    </CardBody>
  </Card>
</Sidebar>

dont.caption: The important content squeezed into the narrow side.
dont.code:
<Sidebar
  sideWidth="sm"
  side={
    <Card>
      <CardBody>
        <Text>Activity, newest first, with every change to the record.</Text>
      </CardBody>
    </Card>
  }
>
  <Card>
    <CardHeader title="Owner" level={4} />
  </Card>
</Sidebar>

accessibility: Layout only: it adds no landmark. For a page’s nav or aside regions use `PageLayout`, which does.
Stacks in DOM order on narrow containers, so nothing is lost at 400% zoom.

exports.name: Skeleton
exports.description: Placeholder for content on first load. Hidden from assistive tech: mark the region that is loading with aria-busy="true" and say what is loading in text (a status line or Spinner label). On refresh keep the existing content instead; never swap usable values for skeletons. The pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion (motion.pulse collapses to 0ms).

props.name: shape
props.description: Mirror the shape of what is loading: lines of text, a block (card, chart), or a table row.

props.name: lines
props.description: text: number of lines. The last one is shorter, like a paragraph.

props.name: columns
props.description: table-row: number of cells. Render inside TableBody, under the real header.

whenToUse: The first load of content whose layout is known: text lines, a card or chart block, table rows under the real header.
Mirror the shape of what is coming so nothing jumps when it arrives.

whenNotToUse.situation: A short action such as saving

do.caption: Keep the real card and heading; only the content that is loading is a skeleton.
do.code:
<Card>
  <CardBody>
    <Skeleton lines={3} />
  </CardBody>
</Card>

dont.caption: One big block for a page of mixed content: it says nothing about what is coming.

accessibility: Skeletons are hidden from assistive tech; the region that is loading should say so (for example `aria-busy` on it).
The pulse stops under reduced motion.

exports.name: Slider
exports.description: Picks a number, or a range, on a continuous scale where the exact value matters less than the position: volume, a price filter. Every thumb is keyboard operable (arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End) and says its value in words; a click on the track moves the nearest thumb, so no drag is needed. For an exact number use a TextField. Behaviour from Radix Slider.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label and accessible name: what the value is ("Price", "Volume"). Required.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the first thumb, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.

props.name: value
props.description: One value for a single slider, two for a range.

props.name: onValueCommit
props.description: Called once when the user lets go or finishes a key press: the moment to save or refetch.

props.name: minStepsBetweenThumbs
props.description: Least number of steps between the two thumbs of a range.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: A value in words ("£40", "40%"). Shown beside the track and read out as aria-valuetext.

props.name: thumbLabels
props.description: Range only: the names of the two thumbs, appended to the label ("Price, minimum").

props.name: name
props.description: Submits each thumb's value as a hidden input with this name.

whenToUse: A value on a continuous scale where position matters more than the exact number: volume, a price filter, a threshold.
A range: pass two values in `defaultValue` (or `value`), and name the thumbs with `thumbLabels`.
Say the value in words with `formatValue` (“£40”, “40%”); it is shown beside the track and read out for each thumb.
Refetch or save on `onValueCommit` (once, when the user lets go), not on every `onValueChange`.

whenNotToUse.situation: An exact number (a quantity, an amount)

do.caption: A labelled range with its value in words; every thumb works with arrow keys.
do.code: <Slider label="Price" defaultValue={[20, 80]} max={200} step={5} formatValue={(v) => `£${String(v)}`} />

dont.caption: A slider for an exact figure: hitting 1,250 by dragging is tedious. Use a field.

accessibility: Each thumb is a `slider` with `aria-valuetext` from `formatValue`; in a range each is named “label, minimum” and “label, maximum”.
Keyboard: arrows move one step, Page Up/Down ten, Home/End to the ends. A click on the track moves the nearest thumb, so no drag is needed (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7).
Thumbs are `size.target-min` (24px). `description` and `error` use the shared field anatomy; `id` lands on the first thumb.

exports.name: Source
exports.definition: interface Source { title: string; origin: string; excerpt?: string; href?: string; hrefLabel?: string; }

exports.name: SourcesList
exports.description: The numbered sources behind an answer, one card each (title, origin, excerpt, a link to the source). Citations in the text point here; the one followed last is marked with aria-current.

props.name: id
props.description: Id that Citations point at (their `sources` prop). Use a useId() value: it must be unique on the page.

props.name: label
props.description: Heading above the list.

props.name: active
props.description: The source last followed from a Citation (1-based): marked as current.

props.name: summary
props.description: Rendered after the heading, before the list (a provenance line: "Based on 1 record and 3 activity entries").

exports.name: Spinner
exports.description: Indeterminate progress for short or briefly unpredictable waits. Longer, shaped waits get a Skeleton.

props.name: label
props.description: Standalone use: what is loading ("Loading records"). Renders a status region that announces it. Omit inside a control that already has a name (Button does): the spinner is then decorative.

whenToUse: Short waits of unknown length where the shape of the result isn’t known.
Inside a pending button, through `Button loading` rather than directly.

whenNotToUse.situation: Loading a page, list or card whose layout is known

do.caption: The pending state belongs to the button that started it.
do.code: <Button loading>Save changes</Button>

dont.caption: A spinner standing in for a whole list: the page jumps when the rows arrive.

accessibility: A standalone spinner takes a `label` and is announced as a status; inside a button it is decorative and the label stays.
It keeps turning under reduced motion: it is the only sign of progress.

exports.name: SplitView
exports.description: A list and the selected item side by side (an inbox, a queue, a file browser), each pane scrolling on its own. The divider resizes the list: drag it, focus it and use ← → (Home and End for the limits), or click it to step through preset widths. Below the size.breakpoint.sm container width it collapses to one pane, the one `show` names, with a Back button above the detail. It lays out; the page owns selection and what the panes hold.

props.name: list
props.description: The list: rows to move through.

props.name: detail
props.description: The selected item, beside the list.

props.name: listLabel
props.description: Accessible names of the two regions ("Conversations", "Conversation"). Required.

props.name: show
props.description: On a narrow container only one pane fits: which one shows. Wide containers always show both. Show the detail once something is opened, the list again on Back.

props.name: onBack
props.description: Narrow only: the Back button above the detail. Omit onBack to leave it out.

props.name: listSize
props.description: The list pane's width in percent (25–65). Uncontrolled default 40.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the divider.

whenToUse: Working through a list one item at a time without losing your place: an inbox, a review queue, support tickets, a file browser.
When people move between neighbouring items often (j and k), so opening each on its own page would cost a round trip.

whenNotToUse.situation: A list people scan and filter, then open one thing
whenNotToUse.instead: the list page (`ListPage`) and a record page

whenNotToUse.situation: A record with properties beside it

do.caption: Both regions named; the page keeps the selection (in the URL) and passes `show` for narrow screens.
do.code:
<SplitView
  listLabel="Conversations"
  detailLabel="Conversation"
  list={<Text>Northwind renewal · Contoso invoice · …</Text>}
  detail={<Text>Northwind renewal: the conversation.</Text>}
/>

dont.caption: Two boxes side by side by hand: no resizing, no keyboard, and on a phone both squeeze into half a screen.

accessibility: Each pane is a named region and scrolls on its own, with the scroll-padding tokens so focus is never hidden at its edges.

The divider is a focusable separator (aria-valuenow is the list’s width in percent): ← → resize by 5%, Home and End go to the limits; a click steps through preset widths, the single-pointer alternative to dragging (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7).
Below the sm breakpoint it collapses to one pane; `onBack` adds a Back button above the detail. Move focus into the detail when it opens, and back to the row on Back.

exports.name: Stack
exports.description: Vertical flow with consistent spacing. The parent owns the space between siblings.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between children. Token-typed: raw values are not accepted.

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis alignment of children.

whenToUse: Anything that flows top to bottom: page sections, form fields, a card body.
Pick the `gap` from the scale; pass `as` for semantics (`section`, `form`, `ul`, `dl`).

whenNotToUse.situation: Equal items that should reflow into columns

do.caption: One Stack owns the rhythm of the form; the fields bring no margins of their own.
do.code:
<Stack as="form" gap="md" align="start" aria-label="Invite">
  <TextField label="Name" />
  <TextField label="Email" type="email" />
  <Button type="submit">Send invite</Button>
</Stack>

dont.caption: Nested Stacks with mixed gaps for the same rhythm: spacing drifts field by field.
dont.code:
<Stack gap="2xs" aria-label="Invite">
  <Stack gap="xl">
    <TextField label="Name" />
  </Stack>
  <TextField label="Email" type="email" />
</Stack>

accessibility: Layout only: it adds no roles. Use `as` so the element matches the content (a list is a `ul`).
Visual order is DOM order, so reading and focus order stay aligned.

exports.name: Stat
exports.description: One headline number in a tile: label, value and an optional change. The change shows its direction as an icon and says it in words to assistive tech; its colour (tone) only adds whether that is good or bad.

props.name: label
props.description: What is counted ("Active records"). Required.

props.name: value
props.description: The number, formatted for the locale ("1,284", "$1.2M"). Tabular figures.

props.name: comparison
props.description: What the delta compares against ("vs previous 30 days").

props.name: directionLabels
props.description: Words read before the delta, per direction. Visually the icon carries it.

whenToUse: A headline number on a dashboard or overview: a count, a total, a rate, with an optional change and what it compares against.
Set `delta.direction` from the numbers (up, down, flat) and `delta.tone` from what it means (positive, negative, neutral): fewer overdue records is down and positive.
Put several in a `Switcher`, so they sit in one row or one column, never a ragged wrap.

whenNotToUse.situation: A value among a record’s properties
whenNotToUse.instead: a definition list in the record’s aside

do.caption: Direction from the numbers, tone from the meaning, and what the change compares against.
do.code:
<Switcher threshold="xs">
  <Stat label="Overdue records" value="14" delta={{ value: '3', direction: 'up', tone: 'negative' }} comparison="vs previous 30 days" />
  <Stat label="Pending approvals" value="9" delta={{ value: '25%', direction: 'down', tone: 'positive' }} comparison="vs previous 30 days" />
</Switcher>

dont.caption: A bare number in coloured text: no label, no comparison, and the colour is the only hint of whether it is good.

accessibility: The direction is an icon plus a visually hidden word (“Up”, “Down”, “No change”; set with `directionLabels`); tone colour only adds good or bad, never carries it alone.
Values use tabular figures, so columns of stats line up.
Format numbers for the locale before passing them; the tile doesn’t format.

exports.name: StatDelta
exports.definition: interface StatDelta { value: string; direction: StatDirection; tone?: StatTone; }

exports.name: StatTone
exports.description: Whether the change is good news. Separate from direction: fewer overdue records is down and positive.

exports.name: Stepper
exports.description: Where someone is in an ordered task. An ordered list: completed steps show a check and a hidden "Completed" prefix, the current one has aria-current="step" and a heavier mark, upcoming ones their number. State is never carried by colour alone. Not navigation: steps are not links.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the list ("Setup steps"). Required.

props.name: current
props.description: Index (from 0) of the step being done now. Earlier steps are completed, later ones upcoming.

props.name: completedLabel
props.description: Visually hidden prefix read before a completed step's label.

whenToUse: Showing where someone is in a task whose steps must be done in order: setup, a multi-step create. Pair it with `FocusedLayout` and copy the Setup wizard example.
Three to six steps with short, parallel labels. Keep the list the same on every step.

whenNotToUse.situation: Sections that can be visited in any order
A form with a few sections
whenNotToUse.instead: one page with cards (the Create and edit example)

do.caption: An ordered list: done steps show a check, the current one is marked, the rest show their number.
do.code: <Stepper label="Setup steps (do example)" steps={steps} current={2} />

dont.caption: Ordered steps as navigation tabs: it suggests people can jump to Plan before naming the workspace.
dont.code:
<NavTabs
  label="Setup steps (don’t example)"
  current="/setup/workspace"
  items={steps.map((s) => ({ label: s.label, href: `/setup/${s.label.toLowerCase()}` }))}
/>

accessibility: An ordered list named by the required `label`; the current step has `aria-current="step"`.
Completed steps read “Completed: <label>” (a visually hidden prefix, set with `completedLabel`) and show a check; state is never colour alone.
Steps are not links. Going back is the page’s Back button or a review step’s Edit.

exports.name: StreamStatus
exports.description: Where an answer is: waiting for its first token, arriving, finished, stopped by the person, or failed.

exports.name: StreamingText
exports.description: Text that arrives token by token (an AI answer), rendered as safe Markdown with a caret while it streams. It holds no timers: the parent appends to `text`, so a story or test can pin any moment. Screen readers hear it through one polite live region, present from mount: "Generating…", then each sentence or paragraph once it is complete (never token by token, and never the whole answer again at the end), then "Stopped" if the person stops it. Text already there on mount (history) is not announced.

props.name: text
props.description: Everything received so far, as Markdown. The parent appends tokens; this renders what it's given.

props.name: citation
props.description: Renders a numbered citation ([1]) found in the text, usually a Citation.

props.name: pendingLabel
props.description: Shown, and announced, before the first token arrives.

props.name: stoppedLabel
props.description: Announced when the person stops the answer.

props.name: codeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of code blocks in the answer.
